grounded_facts: The doctor asserts that Hazel is depressed despite her repeated denials.
memories.memory_text: I heard the doctor say I'm depressed, even though I kept saying I'm not, and it felt like no one was listening to me.

grounded_facts: A medical appointment where Hazel's condition is discussed by her mother and the doctor.
memories.memory_text: I was there in the living room with my mom and the doctor, sitting through another appointment where they talked about my condition while I just wanted to go back to my book.

grounded_facts: Hazel narrates that her depression is not due to cancer but to the fact of dying.
memories.memory_text: I narrated that my depression isn't a side effect of cancer—it's a side effect of dying.

grounded_facts: Hazel repeatedly insists she is not depressed, countering the doctor's diagnosis.
memories.memory_text: I kept telling myself and everyone else that I'm not depressed, because I know my feelings come from the reality of dying, not from the cancer itself.

grounded_facts: Hazel briefly watches a playful couple at Starbucks before returning to her book.
memories.memory_text: I looked up from my book when I heard a laugh, saw a guy spinning a girl around playfully, and then I went back to reading.

grounded_facts: The doctor considers switching Hazel's medication to Zoloft or Lexapro with increased frequency.
memories.memory_text: The doctor told me he might switch me to Zoloft or Lexapro and have me take it twice a day instead of once.

grounded_facts: Hazel sarcastically responds to the doctor's suggestion of increasing medication, comparing herself to Keith Richards.
memories.memory_text: When the doctor suggested increasing my medication, I shot back with 'Why stop there?' and said I could take it—I'm like the Keith Richards of cancer kids.

grounded_facts: A medical consultation involving Hazel, her mother Frannie, and the doctor, focusing on mental health and treatment options.
memories.memory_text: I was there with my mom and the doctor, talking about my mental health and treatment options, and later he asked if I’d been going to that support group.

grounded_facts: Hazel challenges the doctor's use of the word 'journey' to describe illness, showing resistance to euphemistic language.
memories.memory_text: I challenged the doctor when he called my illness a 'journey'—I said, 'Journey? Really?'—because that word felt fake and overused, like it was supposed to make everything sound meaningful.

grounded_facts: The doctor raises the topic of Hazel attending the suggested support group, prompting resistance and skepticism.
memories.memory_text: I remember the doctor asking me again about going to that support group he suggested, and I told him I wasn't sure it was for me, but he kept pushing, saying it would help me connect with others.

grounded_facts: The doctor dismisses Hazel's protest and insists she try the support group, appealing to personal obligation.
memories.memory_text: I remember the doctor dismissing what I said and insisting I try the support group, ending with 'For me'—so I felt I had to agree, even though I didn't want to.

grounded_facts: Hazel participates in a cancer support group meeting in a church basement, where members share their cancer stories.
memories.memory_text: I sat in the church basement during the support group, listening to Patrick talk about being in the heart of Jesus 'literally' while I thought about how he's just exploiting his cancer past, surviving ball cancer but now divorced and addicted to video games, and expecting us to believe we could be like him one day.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Isaac exchange a knowing look of disapproval toward Patrick's speech.
memories.memory_text: I shared a knowing look with Isaac, my only friend here, when Patrick was speaking—we both rolled our eyes at how insincere it felt.

grounded_facts: Patrick calls on Hazel to share her story during the support group session.
memories.memory_text: I remember Patrick gesturing for me to speak, and I felt that familiar dread as I reluctantly stood up.

grounded_facts: Hazel verbally discloses her thyroid cancer with lung metastases during the support group session.
memories.memory_text: I told the group, 'I'm, uh, Hazel. 16. Thyroid originally but with quite the impressive satellite colony in my lungs,' and my voice sounded distant to me.

grounded_facts: The group collectively says 'We're here for you' after Hazel shares her story.
memories.memory_text: After I shared, I heard everyone say together, 'We're here for you,' and I remember thinking how strange it was that they said it like they meant it.

grounded_facts: A gathering of young cancer patients in a church basement led by Patrick, where members share personal experiences with cancer.
memories.memory_text: I was in the church basement with the others, going through the motions of the support group while Patrick led us in saying 'We're here for you'—first for him, then for me.

grounded_facts: Hazel comes out of the church and gets into the car without speaking, only exhaling in response to Frannie's silent question.
Frannie looks at Hazel with a questioning expression; Hazel responds only with an exhale, conveying ambivalence or fatigue.
memories.memory_text: I came out of the church and got in the car, and when Frannie looked at me like she wanted to know how it went, I just exhaled—I didn’t have the energy to say anything.

grounded_facts: A group session takes place inside the church, which Frannie waits for to end and Hazel participates in.
memories.memory_text: I just exhaled and got in the car after the group session inside the church.

grounded_facts: Frannie suggests Hazel call her friends, but Hazel dismisses the idea indifferently.
memories.memory_text: I remember my mom suggesting I call my friends, but I told her that's okay, I didn't feel like it.

grounded_facts: Hazel proposes that her parents go to a movie, encouraging them to take a break from staying home and attending to her.
memories.memory_text: I suggested to my parents that they go to a movie, telling them they haven't been out in a while and they should take the night off to have fun.

grounded_facts: Michael asks if Hazel wants to see a movie, but she redirects the idea to her parents instead.
memories.memory_text: When my dad asked if I wanted to see a movie, I told them they should go instead and have some time to themselves.

grounded_facts: A Friday night family gathering in the living room, centered around passive TV watching and unspoken concern for Hazel.
memories.memory_text: I remember sitting on the couch with my book while 'America's Next Top Model' played, and my parents watched me quietly, not saying much.

grounded_facts: A scheduled gathering for individuals with shared experiences to provide mutual support, which Hazel is being sent to attend.
memories.memory_text: I remember thinking that support group was the worst idea, and I told my parents they couldn't make me go, though I guess they can since they're my parents.

grounded_facts: Hazel's parents insist she attend a support group, overriding her objections.
memories.memory_text: My parents insisted I needed to get out of the house and be a teenager, so they made me go to support group despite my objections.

grounded_facts: Hazel sarcastically rejects the idea of attending support group and suggests getting a fake ID instead.
memories.memory_text: I told my parents that if they really wanted me to be a teenager, they should buy me a fake ID so I could go to clubs and drink gimlets instead of going to support group.

grounded_facts: Frannie ends the discussion by ordering Hazel to get in the car.
memories.memory_text: Frannie ended the argument by telling me to get in the car, so I knew the discussion was over.

grounded_facts: A church service taking place at an Episcopalian sanctuary in suburban Indianapolis.
memories.memory_text: I saw the small Episcopalian sanctuary in suburban Indianapolis when I got out of the car with my mom's help, oxygen tank in tow.

grounded_facts: Hazel goes to a church service at an Episcopalian sanctuary, not out of personal desire but to please her parents.
memories.memory_text: I went to the church service not because I wanted to or thought it would help, but to make my parents happy, like most things I did these days.

grounded_facts: Frannie shouts a suggestion to Hazel to make friends before leaving.
memories.memory_text: I heard my mom shout 'Make some friends!' as she got back in the car, but I didn't feel like engaging with anyone.

grounded_facts: Hazel chooses to take the stairs instead of the elevator after encountering a very sick child.
memories.memory_text: I decided to take the stairs instead of the elevator after seeing that very sick child.

grounded_facts: After bumping into each other, Gus and Hazel exchange brief, polite apologies.
memories.memory_text: I said 'Sorry!' when we bumped into each other, and he replied with 'My bad. No, it's...'—we both apologized so quickly, like we were trying to fix it before it even started.

grounded_facts: Hazel collides with Gus, a strikingly attractive boy, leading to a moment of mutual awareness and speechlessness.
memories.memory_text: I walked right into a supremely beautiful boy, and for a moment, I couldn't speak—I just felt this intense awareness between us before I managed to shuffle away.

grounded_facts: Hazel looks in the mirror and reacts negatively to her own appearance, indicating self-disapproval or distress.
memories.memory_text: I looked in the mirror and didn't like what I saw, feeling a wave of discomfort and self-disapproval.

grounded_facts: A gathering of cancer patients in a church basement for sharing experiences and emotional support.
memories.memory_text: I sat in the Circle of Sick, surrounded by others who, like me, were just trying to get through another day.

grounded_facts: Isaac reveals he will undergo another surgery soon and will likely become blind as a result.
memories.memory_text: I heard Isaac say he was facing another surgery soon and that it would likely leave him blind, and I remember how he tried to downplay it, but I could feel how much it weighed on him.

grounded_facts: Hazel meets Augustus's persistent stare with equal intensity, initiating a silent contest of wills.
memories.memory_text: I felt the Beautiful Boy's gaze on me while Isaac was talking, and it was hard to focus, so I decided to meet his stare head-on.

grounded_facts: Hazel initiates and wins a silent staring contest with Augustus after feeling his persistent gaze.
memories.memory_text: I think I won the staring contest with him because I held my gaze just as firmly, even though I can't be totally sure he gave up first.

grounded_facts: Augustus reveals his name, age, and cancer history, including losing a leg to osteosarcoma and being in remission.
memories.memory_text: I remember Augustus introducing himself, saying he was 17 and had lost a leg to osteosarcoma a year and a half ago, but was now in remission.

grounded_facts: Augustus states that his greatest fear is oblivion, because he wants to live an extraordinary life and be remembered.
memories.memory_text: I heard Augustus say he wants to live an extraordinary life and be remembered, and that his greatest fear is not doing that — it's oblivion.

grounded_facts: Hazel argues that oblivion is inevitable for everyone, and that fearing it is pointless because even great historical figures will eventually be forgotten.
Hazel publicly responds to Augustus's fear of oblivion by arguing it is inevitable and should be ignored.
memories.memory_text: I told Augustus that oblivion is inevitable for everyone, even people like Cleopatra or Mozart, and that fearing it doesn't make sense because eventually no one will remember any of us anyway.

grounded_facts: Augustus tells Hazel she is beautiful, marking the beginning of their romantic tension.
memories.memory_text: He told me I was beautiful, and I remember thinking he must be joking or being sarcastic, but he seemed serious, and it made me feel seen in a way I wasn’t expecting.

grounded_facts: Hazel encounters Augustus (Gus) for the first time outside the church; he approaches her, compliments her, and initiates conversation that leads to a connection.
memories.memory_text: I turned and found this boy, Augustus, standing next to me, and he asked for my full name, which felt intense, and then he told me I was beautiful and said he likes looking at beautiful people because we’re all going to die soon, which caught me off guard.

grounded_facts: A casual gathering outside the church after an event, where teens socialize and couples interact.
memories.memory_text: I was waiting for my mom's car when I saw Isaac making out with Monica across the parking lot, and we both just stood there watching them, which felt kind of awkward and gross.

grounded_facts: Augustus invites Hazel to watch a movie immediately, proposing an impromptu outing.
memories.memory_text: He told me we should watch a movie, and when I didn’t respond right away, he clarified that he meant right then, which surprised me because I hadn’t even agreed to go yet.

grounded_facts: Hazel criticizes Augustus for holding a cigarette, seeing it as self-destructive and hypocritical given his cancer history.
memories.memory_text: I called out Augustus when I saw him with a cigarette, telling him how stupid it was to risk more cancer after everything he'd already been through.

grounded_facts: Augustus shocks Hazel by pulling out a cigarette but explains it is unlit and symbolic — representing control over one's fate despite danger.
memories.memory_text: I saw Augustus pull out a cigarette and got shocked, but then he explained it was never lit—that it was just a metaphor, a way of showing he's in control of his fate even with danger in his mouth.

grounded_facts: Hazel declines her mother's offer to go home, choosing instead to follow through on impromptu plans with Augustus.
memories.memory_text: I told my mom I couldn't go home with her because I'd made plans with Augustus Waters.

grounded_facts: Hazel reacts with sarcasm and dry humor to Gus's admission of being a bad driver.
memories.memory_text: When Gus admitted he was a bad driver, I responded with dry sarcasm, saying 'You don't say' and 'I'm surprised you have a license,' because that’s how I cope with vulnerability.

grounded_facts: Gus admits to failing his driving test multiple times and jokes about his poor driving being a 'cancer perk.'
Gus discloses that he failed his driving test multiple times and barely passed on the fourth attempt, with an instructor deeming his driving 'unpleasant but not technically unsafe.'
memories.memory_text: Gus told me he failed his driving test multiple times and only passed on the fourth try after the instructor said his driving was 'unpleasant but not technically unsafe,' and he joked that having a license was a 'cancer perk.'

grounded_facts: Hazel takes a deep breath and begins recounting the discovery of her cancer, signaling a moment of emotional significance.
memories.memory_text: I take a deep breath and begin to tell the story of how I was diagnosed with cancer, feeling that even though I've told it before, this time is different.

grounded_facts: A car ride during which Hazel and Gus engage in personal conversation while traveling together.
memories.memory_text: I was in the car with Gus, riding together while we talked about personal things, and I could feel the weight of our growing closeness.

grounded_facts: Dad calls emergency services as Hazel struggles to breathe.
memories.memory_text: I could barely breathe, and I saw my dad call 9-1-1 while Frannie stroked my hair.

grounded_facts: Frannie comforts Hazel by running her fingers through her hair as Hazel prepares for a medical procedure.
memories.memory_text: I felt Frannie running her fingers through my hair as I struggled to breathe, trying to calm me down before the procedure.

grounded_facts: Frannie tearfully asks Hazel if she is ready, likely referring to a medical procedure or transition.
memories.memory_text: I remember my mom Frannie asking me tearfully if I was ready, her voice trembling as she leaned close, and I could tell she was trying to stay strong for me.

grounded_facts: Michael becomes overwhelmed with emotion and breaks down, unable to contain his feelings any longer.
memories.memory_text: I saw my dad Michael break down completely, unable to hold back his emotions any longer, and it hurt me to see him so overwhelmed while I was lying there.

grounded_facts: A morning period in the ICU where Hazel shows visible signs of recovery.
memories.memory_text: I remember that morning in the ICU when I started feeling a little more like myself—I was able to eat ice chips, and I noticed the color had come back to my cheeks.

grounded_facts: Hazel begins to recover from her illness as the antibiotics take effect and fluid is drained from her lungs.
memories.memory_text: I know I began to recover because the antibiotics finally kicked in and the doctors drained the fluid from my lungs; I could feel myself getting stronger over time.

grounded_facts: Hazel reveals that her tumors have shrunk and her metastases have barely progressed, indicating a temporary medical stabilization despite ongoing lung issues.
memories.memory_text: I told Gus that my tumors have shrunk and my metastases have hardly grown since the last scan, which means things are stable for now even though my lungs still aren't doing well.

grounded_facts: An informal, intimate conversation between Hazel and Gus during a car ride, serving as emotional and informational bonding time.
memories.memory_text: I remember talking with Gus in the car, just the two of us, sharing quiet moments and words that felt close and real, like we were really seeing each other.

grounded_facts: Gus playfully attributes Hazel's sophistication to her being a college girl after learning she has her GED.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus teasing me, saying I must be a college girl and that’s why I have this ‘aura of sophistication,’ after I told him I had my GED.

grounded_facts: Hazel responds to Gus's joke with a light shove, signaling ease and growing intimacy.
memories.memory_text: I smiled back at Gus and gave him a light shove on his arm, just playful enough to feel like we were really starting to ease into each other.

grounded_facts: Gus successfully drives and parks his car in his driveway, marking the end of the car ride and transition to a new location.
memories.memory_text: I was in the car with Gus when he pulled into his driveway, and I saw him park; he turned to me and said, 'We're here,' marking the end of the ride.

grounded_facts: Gus rolls his eyes when explaining his parents' engraved plaques as 'encouragements', signaling mild embarrassment or affectionate mockery to Hazel.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gus roll his eyes when he called his parents' plaques 'encouragements,' and I could tell he meant it affectionately but also a little mockingly.

grounded_facts: Gus's parents are preparing dinner in the kitchen when Hazel arrives with Gus.
memories.memory_text: When I arrived at Gus's house, I noticed his parents were already busy making dinner in the kitchen.

grounded_facts: Gus brings Hazel into his house and introduces her to his parents, who are making dinner in the kitchen.
memories.memory_text: Gus introduced me to his parents in the kitchen, and I realized they didn’t seem surprised to see him with a girl, which I made a mental note of.

grounded_facts: Hazel clarifies that she goes by 'Hazel', not 'Hazel Grace', asserting her preferred identity.
memories.memory_text: When Gus introduced me as 'Hazel Grace,' I corrected him and said it's just 'Hazel,' because that's what I go by.

grounded_facts: Gus abruptly ends the parental introduction and pulls Hazel downstairs, redirecting focus to private time together.
memories.memory_text: After the quick introduction, Gus abruptly said we were going downstairs and then pulled me into the next room, leaving his parents behind.

grounded_facts: Gus leads Hazel downstairs to his basement bedroom, revealing personal space filled with video games, band posters, and basketball memorabilia.
memories.memory_text: I followed Gus downstairs to his basement bedroom, and I saw it was filled with video games, band posters, and basketball memorabilia—he even pointed out what was really his and what he called 'cancer perks.'

grounded_facts: Hazel struggles with breathing after descending stairs and standing, requiring rest on Gus's bed.
memories.memory_text: I struggled to breathe after walking down the stairs and had to sit on Gus's bed to recover—I told him I'd be fine unless I fainted, joking that I'm a bit of a Victorian lady that way.

grounded_facts: Hazel names 'An Imperial Affliction' as her favorite novel, describing it as deeply meaningful and spiritually significant to her.
memories.memory_text: I told Gus that 'An Imperial Affliction' is my favorite novel—my bible, really—and that its author understands what it’s like to be dying without having died, which means something deep to me.

grounded_facts: Gus commits to reading 'An Imperial Affliction' despite initial skepticism, marking a shift in his attitude toward Hazel's inner world.
memories.memory_text: I saw that Gus decided to read 'An Imperial Affliction' even though he wasn’t sure about it at first, and I realized he was trying to understand my world.

grounded_facts: Gus gives Hazel a novelization of his favorite video game in exchange for her reading 'An Imperial Affliction', forming a symbolic pact.
Their hands briefly tangle when exchanging books, creating a moment of romantic tension and connection.
memories.memory_text: I gave Gus my copy of 'An Imperial Affliction' and he handed me a novelization of his favorite video game, and when I took it, our hands got tangled for a brief, charged moment—it felt like a real connection.

grounded_facts: Gus and Hazel have an intimate conversation in his basement bedroom after being introduced to his parents.
memories.memory_text: Down in his basement bedroom, I sat on the bed while Gus sat beside me, and we started talking—really talking—about my favorite book and what it means to me, and I remember feeling both exposed and seen.

grounded_facts: Gus flirts with Hazel by saying he loves it when she talks medical, responding to her explanation of cold hands.
memories.memory_text: I explained why my hands were cold, and Gus flirted with me, saying he loves it when I talk medical—he made me feel seen in a whole new way.

grounded_facts: Hazel is reading a novella written by Gus, indicating he gave her the book, which represents a personal and creative gesture.
memories.memory_text: I think Gus gave me this novella, and reading it feels like a personal thing, something he made just for me, though I'm not sure what it means.

grounded_facts: Hazel insists she is not waiting for Gus to call, despite clear signs of anticipation.
memories.memory_text: I told my mom I'm not waiting for Gus to call—it's no big deal, we just hung out—but even as I said it, I could feel myself hoping my phone would buzz with his name.

grounded_facts: Frannie observes the new book and comments on it, initiating a brief exchange about Gus.
memories.memory_text: Frannie noticed the new book and commented on it, asking if Gus gave it to me, and when I didn't answer, she just stayed quiet in a way that felt like she knew more than I wanted her to.

grounded_facts: Hazel reads Gus's novella in bed at night while Frannie briefly visits the room.
memories.memory_text: I was reading Gus's novella in bed at night when Frannie briefly came into the room, and I kept on not waiting for his call.

grounded_facts: Hazel repeatedly checks her phone while engaging in daily activities, revealing her emotional preoccupation with hearing from Gus.
memories.memory_text: I kept checking my phone while brushing my teeth, eating breakfast, watching TV, and staring out at the rain, trying to pretend I wasn't desperate to hear from him, but I always ended up looking at it again.

grounded_facts: A family dinner at Hazel's home where Hazel receives texts from Gus.
memories.memory_text: I was at dinner with my parents, feeling a bit sullen and pushing food around my plate, when my phone buzzed with a text from Gus.

grounded_facts: Hazel receives a series of texts from Gus about his frustration with a book ending mid-sentence, which visibly affects her mood.
memories.memory_text: I read Gus's frantic texts about his book ending mid-sentence, and even though I tried to stay composed with my parents watching, I couldn't help but laugh out loud at his dramatic reaction.

grounded_facts: Michael notices Hazel's distraction and laughter from the texts, and offers to let her leave the table.
memories.memory_text: I was laughing at Gus's text and wasn't paying attention to dinner, then Michael cleared his throat and asked if I wanted to be excused.

grounded_facts: Hazel initiates a phone call to Gus, who answers immediately.
memories.memory_text: I sat down on the patio chair and dialed Gus, and he answered right away on the first ring.

grounded_facts: During the call, a loud wail is heard from Gus's end, indicating possible emotional or physical distress.
memories.memory_text: During our call, a loud wail came from Gus's side, which made me think he might be in emotional or physical distress.

grounded_facts: After hearing a wail from Gus's end of the line, Hazel immediately checks if he is okay.
memories.memory_text: After hearing that wail, I immediately asked him, 'What the -- are you ok?' because I was worried something was really wrong.

grounded_facts: A phone call initiated by Hazel and received by Gus, beginning with casual banter and interrupted by a sudden emotional outburst.
memories.memory_text: We were talking casually when suddenly I heard a loud wail from his end, and I wasn't sure if it was emotional or something worse.

grounded_facts: Isaac experiences a severe emotional collapse, wailing uncontrollably on Gus's couch.
memories.memory_text: I heard wailing and had no idea what was going on.

grounded_facts: Gus attempts to stabilize the situation by commanding Isaac to focus on him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gus trying to calm Isaac down by telling him to focus on him.

grounded_facts: Gus rhetorically asks Hazel whether her presence or association with the support group would improve or worsen Isaac's state.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus asking me if my being there from support group would make things better or worse for Isaac.

grounded_facts: Gus decides to involve Hazel and asks her how quickly she can arrive at his location.
memories.memory_text: Gus called me and asked how fast I could get to his place.

grounded_facts: An informal support gathering in Gus's basement where Hazel visits Isaac during his emotional crisis following a breakup.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus calling out that I was coming downstairs to his basement, and I followed him into the room where I saw Isaac sitting upside down in his gaming chair with tears on his face, and then Gus gestured for me to sit so we could both be there with Isaac.

grounded_facts: Isaac discloses that Monica ended their relationship, unable to cope with his impending blindness, marking a key emotional turning point in the scene.
memories.memory_text: I heard Isaac say that Monica broke up with him because she couldn't handle his impending blindness, and that he kept saying 'always' but she wouldn't say it back, like he was already gone.

grounded_facts: Hazel physically and verbally supports Isaac after he reveals his heartbreak.
memories.memory_text: I asked Isaac if he wanted to talk about it, I rubbed his shoulder to comfort him, and I told him that sometimes people don't understand the promises they're making when they make them.

grounded_facts: Gus quotes a line from Hazel's favorite book, leading to mutual recognition and emotional connection.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Gus quotes a line from Hazel's favorite book, leading to mutual recognition and emotional connection.

grounded_facts: Gus reveals his deep engagement with 'An Imperial Affliction' and his wish to contact its reclusive author, Peter Van Houten, initiating a shared intellectual bond with Hazel.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Gus reveals his deep engagement with 'An Imperial Affliction' and his wish to contact its reclusive author, Peter Van Houten, initiating a shared intellectual bond with Hazel.

grounded_facts: Gus hands Isaac a trophy and nods, giving him implicit permission to break it as a form of emotional release.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gus hand Isaac one of his basketball trophies, and after looking at it like he wasn't sure what to do, Isaac glanced at Gus as if asking for permission—then smashed it when Gus nodded.

grounded_facts: With Gus's encouragement, Isaac transitions from passive grief to physical release by destroying Gus's basketball trophies, symbolizing emotional catharsis.
memories.memory_text: I think Isaac started destroying the trophies because Gus encouraged him, and it seemed like a way for Isaac to let go of some pain—he went from hesitating to grabbing more and smashing them, and I remember Gus saying afterward that pain demands to be felt, which made me wonder if this was really helping Isaac release everything he'd been holding in.

grounded_facts: Hazel has dinner with her parents, Frannie and Michael.
memories.memory_text: I was having dinner with my parents, Frannie and Michael, like we often do.

grounded_facts: Dr. Maria scheduled Hazel's PET scan for the eighth.
memories.memory_text: I was told by my mom that Dr. Maria called and scheduled my PET scan for the eighth.

grounded_facts: Hazel is actually eating, which her parents notice and react to positively.
memories.memory_text: I was eating dinner, and I noticed my parents watching me with quiet relief, their eyes a little brighter than usual.

grounded_facts: Frannie tells Michael that Support Group was a good idea, implying it contributed to Hazel's better state.
memories.memory_text: I heard Frannie tell Michael that Support Group was a good idea, as if that’s what’s helping me feel better lately.

grounded_facts: Hazel's phone buzzes with a message from Augustus, prompting her to seek permission to respond.
memories.memory_text: I felt my phone buzz and saw it was a message from Augustus, so I looked to my parents for permission before responding.

grounded_facts: Michael allows Hazel to answer or respond to Augustus's message.
memories.memory_text: I heard Michael say 'By all means,' so I knew he was giving me permission to answer Augustus.

grounded_facts: A shared imaginative act where Gus pretends to read an official email from Peter Van Houten in response to Hazel's earlier expressed desire for closure about the novel.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Gus pretended to read an email from Peter Van Houten, responding to my deepest wish for closure about the novel.

grounded_facts: Gus pretends to read an email response from Peter Van Houten to Hazel, claiming the author has refused to write a sequel.
Gus fabricates a letter from Van Houten to emotionally engage Hazel, surprising her with a simulated response to her deepest literary longing.
memories.memory_text: Gus told me he had contacted Van Houten's assistant and received a reply, and I remember him asking if I believed he could make up a letter from the great author, which made me realize he was pretending.

grounded_facts: Hazel expresses shock, hope, and excitement in response to the fabricated letter, validating Gus's emotional intent.
memories.memory_text: I felt a surge of shock and hope when I first heard the letter, and I remember jumping up as fast as my lungs would let me, saying 'Holy hell,' caught between disbelief and excitement.

grounded_facts: After hearing the fabricated letter, Hazel jumps up to check her inbox upon Gus's suggestion.
memories.memory_text: I jumped up as fast as my lungs would allow to check my inbox after Gus told me about the letter, because I really wanted to see if Van Houten had actually written back.

grounded_facts: Hazel spends the night composing a letter to Van Houten while on the phone with Augustus, who listens and provides feedback.
Hazel reads her draft email aloud to Augustus to get his opinion on tone and content.
Hazel composes and reads aloud an email to Peter Van Houten, asking for answers about the aftermath of his novel and expressing deep admiration.
memories.memory_text: I spent the night composing an email to Peter Van Houten while on the phone with Augustus, and I read it aloud to him so he could give me feedback on the tone and content.

grounded_facts: Augustus evaluates Hazel's email as well-written and suitable for Van Houten's style, despite minor pretentiousness.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Augustus that my email was well-written and suitable for Van Houten's style, even if it was a bit pretentious.

grounded_facts: After finishing the email, Hazel and Augustus prolong their phone call, exchanging multiple 'ok's, delaying the end of the interaction.
Hazel and Augustus repeatedly say 'ok' instead of hanging up, creating a tender, intimate ritual.
memories.memory_text: After we finished the email, I didn't want to hang up with Augustus, so we kept saying 'ok' to each other instead of ending the call, and it turned into this tender little ritual where I smiled when he said maybe 'ok' could be our 'always.'

grounded_facts: After Gus hangs up, Hazel reflects on whether Augustus genuinely likes her, expressing internal doubt.
memories.memory_text: After Gus hung up, I wondered if it was really possible that this beautiful boy actually likes me—I thought about it, but I'm not convinced.

grounded_facts: Isaac is now officially blind, with bandages covering his eyes.
memories.memory_text: I saw Isaac lying in bed with bandages over his eyes, and I knew he was officially blind now.

grounded_facts: Hazel visits Isaac in the hospital recovery room during the day.
memories.memory_text: I visited Isaac in the hospital during the day and sat by his side while a nurse attended to him.

grounded_facts: Isaac voices his pain that Monica has not visited him since his injury.
memories.memory_text: I heard Isaac say that Monica hadn't visited him since his injury, and he sounded really hurt by it.

grounded_facts: Isaac and Hazel joke about qualities of a good nurse, bonding through dark humor.
memories.memory_text: I joked with Isaac about what makes a good nurse, like not punning your disability or saying 'little ouchie' before stabbing you with a needle, and we both laughed.

grounded_facts: Isaac expresses his belief in true love despite physical suffering.
memories.memory_text: I remember Isaac telling me that even though people suffer, everyone should have true love.

grounded_facts: Isaac uses his pain pump to administer morphine, leading to drowsiness and sleep.
memories.memory_text: I saw Isaac press the button on his pain pump, and I watched as the morphine made him drowsy until he fell asleep.

grounded_facts: Isaac begins to share information about Gus's visit but falls asleep before completing the thought.
memories.memory_text: I asked Isaac what about Gus, but he was already falling asleep and didn’t get to finish what he was going to say.

grounded_facts: Hazel discovers a response from the reclusive author Peter Van Houten, who refuses to answer her questions in writing but invites her to visit him in Amsterdam.
memories.memory_text: I discovered Peter Van Houten had responded to me—he wouldn't answer my questions in writing, but he said if I ever found myself in Amsterdam, I should pay him a visit, and I just screamed, 'Son of a—WHAT IS THIS LIFE!!!'

grounded_facts: Hazel shares the email from Peter Van Houten with her mother, seeking validation and support.
memories.memory_text: I showed my mom the email from Peter Van Houten and waited for her to read it, hoping she’d understand how much it meant to me.

grounded_facts: Hazel asks her mother Frannie to go to Amsterdam to meet Peter Van Houten after receiving his email.
memories.memory_text: I asked my mom if we could go to Amsterdam to meet Peter Van Houten, and I pleaded with her, saying please.

grounded_facts: Frannie explains that they cannot afford the trip to Amsterdam, including the cost of medical equipment transport.
Frannie tells Hazel they cannot afford the trip to Amsterdam, emphasizing her love despite the limitation.
memories.memory_text: I heard my mom explain that we couldn't afford the trip to Amsterdam, especially with the cost of getting my medical equipment there, and she told me she loved me even though we couldn't make it happen.

grounded_facts: Hazel tells her mother not to do anything and to forget the request, alleviating Frannie's guilt.
memories.memory_text: I told my mom not to do anything and to forget I ever asked about going to Amsterdam, because I saw how upset she was.

grounded_facts: After seeing her mother's distress, Hazel retracts her request and tells her mother not to take further action, internalizing guilt.
memories.memory_text: After seeing how much my mom was struggling, I think I pulled back from asking to go to Amsterdam to spare her, though I still feel like it's my fault she’s carrying this burden.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus walk together on a suburban sidewalk, engaging in personal conversation.
memories.memory_text: I walked side by side with Gus on the sidewalk, just talking as we went.

grounded_facts: Hazel discloses that she used her wish to visit Disney World and Epcot Center when she was 13.
memories.memory_text: I told Gus that I used my wish to go to Disney World and Epcot Center when I was 13.

grounded_facts: Gus mocks Hazel for using her wish on Disney World, calling it cliché and sad.
memories.memory_text: I heard Gus call my wish cliché and sad, mocking me for choosing Disney.

grounded_facts: Hazel is surprised and flustered upon hearing Gus has a crush on her, blushing and trying to hide her excitement.
memories.memory_text: I felt my face flush when he said 'crush'—I looked away fast, heart racing, and couldn't focus on anything else he said after that.

grounded_facts: Gus unintentionally reveals he has a crush on Hazel, causing emotional shift in their interaction.
memories.memory_text: I heard Gus say, 'How can I have a crush on a girl with such cliche wishes?' and I realized he was talking about me, though it came out almost like a joke.

grounded_facts: Hazel is being scanned in a PET machine, following standard procedure instructions from a technician.
memories.memory_text: I was being fed into the PET scan machine while a technician told me to hold still and try to relax, so I did my best to follow the instructions.

grounded_facts: Gus is already waiting on the front stoop when Frannie's car pulls up, indicating his arrival prior to the family's return from the hospital.
memories.memory_text: Gus was already sitting on the front stoop when Mom's car pulled up, so he must have arrived before we got back from the hospital.

grounded_facts: An informal and unanticipated gathering at Hazel's house upon her return from the hospital, initiated by Gus's presence.
memories.memory_text: When I saw Gus rise to help me out of the car, with Mom and Michael there too, it turned our return from the hospital into this unplanned little gathering at my house.

grounded_facts: Gus brings a bouquet of bright orange tulips and is present with them when Hazel arrives, implying the gift is intended for her.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gus waiting on the stoop when we got home, wearing a Pacers jersey and holding bright orange tulips, and he stood up to help me out of the car, making it feel like he brought the flowers just for me.

grounded_facts: Gus acknowledges Hazel upon her arrival with a simple 'Hi Hazel,' following her surprised reaction.
memories.memory_text: I heard Gus say 'Hi Hazel' when I arrived, right after I noticed him.

grounded_facts: Gus asks Hazel if she would like to go on a picnic, marking a direct romantic or social overture.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus asking me, 'How would you like to go on a picnic?'—it felt like a direct invitation, though I wasn't sure what he really meant.

grounded_facts: Hazel gets ready for a date with Gus while others wait downstairs.
memories.memory_text: I got ready for my date with Gus while the others waited downstairs, putting on lip gloss and arranging the orange flowers in a toothbrush holder.

grounded_facts: Gus discloses that he has been sober for fourteen months.
memories.memory_text: I overheard part of the conversation downstairs and inferred that Gus has been sober for fourteen months, though I wasn't sure of the exact details.

grounded_facts: Michael informs Gus that Hazel is still very sick and will be for the rest of her life, particularly noting her lung condition.
memories.memory_text: I overheard my dad telling Gus that I'm still very sick and will be for the rest of my life, especially because of my lungs.

grounded_facts: Hazel asks Gus if he is ready, signaling the transition from waiting to departure.
memories.memory_text: I asked Gus if he was ready, making sure we could leave right then and start our date.

grounded_facts: Hazel appears and asks Gus if he is ready, cutting off Michael's sentence about her health.
memories.memory_text: I heard my dad saying I'm still pretty sick and will be the rest of my life, but I didn't want that to define the moment, so I interrupted.

grounded_facts: Gus explains that it wouldn't make sense to meet Peter Van Houten without Hazel, acknowledging her central role in his literary journey.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus saying it wouldn't make much sense for him to meet Peter Van Houten without me, since I was the one who introduced him to the book, and that made me feel like I was really part of his journey.

grounded_facts: Gus uses a stick to draw circles in the dirt to humorously illustrate the rarity of 17-year-old guys with one leg who are still virgins.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gus pick up a stick and draw a big circle in the dirt to joke about how rare it is for a 17-year-old guy with one leg to still be a virgin, and he said he got it in exchange for his leg and that the Genies agreed.

grounded_facts: Hazel pauses the romantic moment to ask if Gus is only taking her to Amsterdam to get kissed.
memories.memory_text: I paused the moment and asked Gus if he was only taking me to Amsterdam so I'd kiss him.

grounded_facts: After questioning Gus's motives, Hazel initiates a kiss, confirming mutual romantic feelings.
memories.memory_text: I told Gus I'd kiss him either way, and then I did, confirming how I truly felt about him.

grounded_facts: Gus reveals that he saved his wish and intends to use it to go to Amsterdam with Hazel to meet Peter Van Houten.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus telling me he still had his wish saved and that he got it in exchange for his leg, and then he said it wouldn't make much sense to meet Peter Van Houten without me, and that the Genies agreed—we were leaving on May third to go to Amsterdam to meet Peter Van Houten, because he found his wish in me.

grounded_facts: Gus states that meeting Hazel was his true wish, transforming the emotional meaning of the trip.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus saying, 'Because Hazel Grace... I found my Wish,' and in that moment, I felt truly seen—like I wasn't just a side effect of his journey, but the whole point.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus share a picnic in the gardens behind the Indianapolis Museum of Art, discussing life, literature, and love.
memories.memory_text: I remember sitting with Gus on a blanket behind the museum, eating sandwiches and watching kids play on the giant bones while we talked about life and love, and I was so moved that I hugged him.

grounded_facts: Frannie refuses Hazel's request to accept a gift from someone she considers a virtual stranger.
memories.memory_text: I asked Frannie to accept the gift, but she refused, saying we couldn't take it from a virtual stranger.

grounded_facts: Hazel counters Frannie's characterization of the man as a stranger by rejecting the implication as inappropriate.
memories.memory_text: When Frannie called him a stranger, I told her not to be gross, because I didn't think that was fair.

grounded_facts: Hazel proposes asking Dr. Maria for guidance regarding the situation with the man from online.
memories.memory_text: I suggested we ask Dr. Maria for guidance, hoping she might help us figure out if it was okay to accept the gift.

grounded_facts: Dr. Maria acknowledges the PET scan results as encouraging but expresses concern about their durability and the risk of traveling abroad.
memories.memory_text: I heard Dr. Maria say the PET scan results were encouraging, but she didn't know how long it would last and worried about what might happen if I got sick in a foreign country.

grounded_facts: Dr. Maria refuses to approve Hazel's travel due to medical uncertainty and lack of case familiarity abroad.
memories.memory_text: I was told outright that traveling wasn't an option, and even though I pushed back, Dr. Maria refused to approve my trip because no one abroad would know my case well enough.

grounded_facts: A scheduled visit between Hazel and her oncologist, Dr. Maria, to discuss her latest PET scan results and health outlook.
memories.memory_text: I went to my oncologist Dr. Maria for a visit to talk about my latest PET scan results and what they meant for my health.

grounded_facts: Hazel insists on going to Amsterdam and proposes that her mother accompany her, leveraging the Genies' financial resources.
Hazel pressures her mother to agree to travel to Amsterdam by appealing to her curiosity and financial feasibility.
memories.memory_text: I insisted on going to Amsterdam and asked my mom to come with me, telling her the Genies could cover it since they're loaded, and I reminded her she's never been there before.

grounded_facts: Hazel wakes up screaming, shaking, and holding her head, indicating a traumatic nightmare or psychological distress.
memories.memory_text: I woke up screaming in the middle of the night, shaking and holding my head.

grounded_facts: Frannie signals to Michael to leave and call for assistance following Hazel's distressing episode.
memories.memory_text: I saw Mom signal to Michael to leave and call for help while I was still crying.

grounded_facts: Frannie stays with Hazel, rocking her and promising that the nightmare will end, offering maternal comfort.
memories.memory_text: I remember Mom staying with me, rocking me and promising that it would all be okay after the nightmare.

grounded_facts: Michael attempts to maintain composure while driving under emotionally taxing circumstances.
memories.memory_text: I saw Michael driving, trying so hard to keep it together, his silence heavy with effort.

grounded_facts: Hazel remains in a state of silent screaming, indicating ongoing physical or psychological distress.
memories.memory_text: I was screaming silently, my body gripped by pain or terror, though I couldn't make a sound.

grounded_facts: Hazel is brought into the emergency room by Michael and immediately attended by doctors due to her critical condition.
A medical emergency involving Hazel's urgent admission and treatment in the hospital's emergency room.
memories.memory_text: I was carried into the emergency room by Michael, and I remember the chaos as doctors rushed toward me because I was in such bad shape.

grounded_facts: Hazel uses voiceover to directly express her desire to die, creating an intimate moment of emotional disclosure.
In a voiceover, Hazel expresses a deep emotional surrender, stating she would have been happy to die in that moment.
memories.memory_text: I used my voiceover to tell the audience how I felt in that moment — I would have been very, very happy to die, and I wanted them to know it.

grounded_facts: The nurse comforts Hazel upon waking by confirming she is okay.
memories.memory_text: I heard the nurse tell me, 'You're ok, Hazel,' and felt comforted as I came around.

grounded_facts: Hazel's parents enter the room crying and kiss her repeatedly, expressing overwhelming relief at her survival.
memories.memory_text: I saw my parents burst into the room, crying, and they kissed me over and over, saying how relieved they were that I was still here.

grounded_facts: A medical follow-up occasion in the ICU where Hazel's condition is assessed after a critical episode involving lung fluid accumulation.
memories.memory_text: I remember seeing the tube in my side draining fluid, and knowing the doctors were checking my condition after the buildup in my lungs.

grounded_facts: Medical staff drained a significant amount of fluid (1.5 liters) from Hazel's lungs, resolving oxygenation issues.
memories.memory_text: I felt the tube in my side and saw the fluid draining into the bag, and I knew they had taken out a lot of fluid to help me breathe again.

grounded_facts: Frannie informs Hazel about the fluid in her lungs and the drainage procedure.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Frannie that there had been fluid in my lungs stopping me from getting enough oxygen, and that they drained a liter and a half the night before.

grounded_facts: Michael tells Hazel there is no tumor growth, bringing emotional relief.
Hazel is informed by her parents that there is no tumor growth or new tumors in her body, providing significant medical relief.
memories.memory_text: I remember Michael and my parents telling me there was no tumor growth and no new tumors in my body, and I felt a wave of relief wash over me.

grounded_facts: Hazel regains consciousness in the hospital ICU after a critical health event, indicated by the returning sound of a heart monitor and her opening eyes.
memories.memory_text: I heard the beeping of a heart monitor and realized I was back, my eyes opening in the ICU with relief.

grounded_facts: Frannie hugs her daughter to comfort her and affirm their bond after the medical crisis.
memories.memory_text: I felt my mom hug me tightly, and in that moment, I knew she was comforting me and holding me close after everything I'd been through.

grounded_facts: A formal meeting between Hazel, her parents, and her full oncology team to discuss the status and future of her treatment.
memories.memory_text: I sat at a large conference table with my parents and my full oncology team for a formal meeting about my treatment.

grounded_facts: Hazel's tumor growth is being controlled by the drug Phalanxifor.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Phalanxifor is still controlling my tumor growth, which was a relief to hear.

grounded_facts: Serious fluid accumulation (edema) is identified as a worsening side effect of Phalanxifor.
memories.memory_text: I was informed that serious fluid accumulation is getting worse as a side effect of Phalanxifor, and I remember feeling uneasy about that.

grounded_facts: Hazel responds to a question about treatment direction by stating she feels unqualified to make the decision.
memories.memory_text: I said I felt unqualified to make the decision about my treatment direction.

grounded_facts: Doctors acknowledge uncertainty about continuing Phalanxifor due to unknown long-term effects and lack of precedent.
memories.memory_text: I heard the doctors say they don't really know the long-term effects of Phalanxifor because so few people have been on it as long as I have.

grounded_facts: Hazel's request for a lung transplant is gently rejected due to her being an unsuitable candidate.
memories.memory_text: I was told I wouldn't be considered a strong candidate for a lung transplant, and those words just hung there, heavy and final.

grounded_facts: Michael becomes emotional upon hearing Hazel cannot get a transplant and seeks comfort by holding Frannie's hand.
memories.memory_text: I saw my dad reach for Mom's hand right after, gripping it tight like he needed her to stay together.

grounded_facts: Hazel watches her parents holding hands and trying not to cry, which causes her emotional pain and guilt.
memories.memory_text: I kept watching them hold hands and try not to cry, and it made me feel guilty for putting that pain in their eyes.

grounded_facts: Frannie asks Hazel if she is ready for the procedure, showing maternal concern.
memories.memory_text: I remember my mom asking me if I was ready for the procedure, her voice full of concern.

grounded_facts: Frannie speaks emotionally after Hazel loses consciousness, declaring she won't be a mom anymore, which Hazel overhears.
memories.memory_text: I overheard my mom say, 'I won't be a mom anymore,' right after I started losing consciousness during the procedure.

grounded_facts: Hazel interrupts the medical discussion to ask if she can still travel to Amsterdam, signaling her desire to pursue meaningful experiences despite her illness.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Hazel interrupts the medical discussion to ask if she can still travel to Amsterdam, signaling her desire to pursue meaningful experiences despite her illness.

grounded_facts: Hazel declares that it's her life, asserting her right to make decisions about her own experiences despite medical risks.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Hazel declares that it's her life, asserting her right to make decisions about her own experiences despite medical risks.

grounded_facts: Hazel persistently questions Dr. Simmons' dismissal of her travel plans, asserting her autonomy and confronting medical authority.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Hazel persistently questions Dr. Simmons' dismissal of her travel plans, asserting her autonomy and confronting medical authority.

grounded_facts: Dr. Simmons explicitly states that Hazel is too sick to travel, delivering a blunt medical reality that crushes her hope.
memories.memory_text: I remember Dr. Simmons looking at me and saying, 'You're just too sick,' and in that moment, I knew I wasn't going to Amsterdam — my hope for traveling just collapsed.

grounded_facts: A formal meeting between Hazel, her family, and doctors to discuss her condition and treatment, during which the possibility of travel is raised and denied.
memories.memory_text: I remember that A formal meeting between Hazel, her family, and doctors to discuss her condition and treatment, during which the possibility of travel is raised and denied.

grounded_facts: Hazel is brought home by her parents after a hospital stay, indicating a recent health or emotional crisis.
memories.memory_text: I remember my parents bringing me home from the hospital, and I know I looked miserable—those few days had taken a real emotional toll on me.

grounded_facts: Gus sends a text message asking Hazel if she is ok, showing concern.
memories.memory_text: I think Gus was checking in because he was concerned about me, but I'm not entirely sure how he really felt.

grounded_facts: Hazel receives a text message from Gus asking 'ok?' but does not respond.
memories.memory_text: I received a text from Gus that just said 'ok?' and I saw it, but I didn't reply.

grounded_facts: Michael tells Hazel that Gus is on the phone, relaying an incoming communication.
memories.memory_text: I remember Michael telling me that Gus was on the phone again.

grounded_facts: Hazel silently refuses to take the phone call from Gus, indicating emotional withdrawal.
Hazel leaves the kitchen and goes into her bedroom, showing signs of depression.
memories.memory_text: I shook my head and didn't take the call, then went into my bedroom because I just couldn't face talking to him—I felt too low.

grounded_facts: Hazel sends a second text clarifying that she sees herself as a source of future pain for Augustus, reinforcing her decision to end the relationship.
memories.memory_text: I sent Augustus a second text because I needed him to understand that I see myself as someone who will only bring him pain, and that’s why I had to end things.

grounded_facts: Hazel uses the metaphor 'I'm a grenade' to express how she believes her death will emotionally destroy those close to her.
memories.memory_text: I told Augustus, 'I'm a grenade,' because I believe my death will tear apart everyone I love.

grounded_facts: Hazel initiates emotional separation by texting Augustus that she can no longer be with him, citing her terminal illness.
memories.memory_text: I texted Augustus that I can't see him anymore, even though I want to, because I can't bear the thought of what my death will put him through.

grounded_facts: Hazel makes the emotional decision to end her relationship with Augustus to protect him from future pain caused by her illness.
memories.memory_text: I think ending things with Augustus might protect him from the pain I’ll cause when I die, but I’m not entirely sure if it’s the right choice.

grounded_facts: Hazel tells Augustus that seeing him makes her anticipate the pain she will cause him when she dies.
memories.memory_text: I told Augustus I can't see him anymore because when I look at him, all I see is the pain I'll cause him when I die—I even said I'm a grenade, and I couldn't bear the thought of hurting him like that.

grounded_facts: After the emotional exchange, Augustus responds to Hazel's 'Ok' with a joking remark about flirting, masking his hurt.
After receiving Hazel's serious messages, Augustus replies with humor to mask his pain, calling her 'flirting' in response to her 'Ok.'
memories.memory_text: I saw Augustus respond to my 'Ok' with a joke, calling me out for flirting, but I knew he was using humor to hide how hurt he really was.

grounded_facts: Gus uses humor to lighten Hazel's mood by demanding to see the 'swing set of tears,' which makes her smile.
memories.memory_text: I remember smiling when Gus said, 'I demand to see this swing set of tears,' because even though I was sad, he made me laugh with that ridiculous line.

grounded_facts: Gus responds to Hazel's call and comes to her backyard, transforming the emotional atmosphere.
memories.memory_text: I heard Gus call out my name when he arrived in the backyard, and his presence immediately made things feel better, like the weight I was carrying started to lift.

grounded_facts: Gus tells Hazel that her attempts to distance herself will not reduce his feelings for her.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus telling me that no matter how hard I try to keep my distance, it won't change his feelings for me.

grounded_facts: Gus names the unspoken fear Hazel carries — that she will emotionally destroy those close to her when she dies — using the metaphor of a grenade.
memories.memory_text: I heard Gus say that I'm like a grenade, and that he understands my fear of hurting everyone close to me when I die.

grounded_facts: Hazel confirms Gus's metaphor that she is a 'grenade' who will emotionally destroy those close to her when she dies.
memories.memory_text: I confirmed to Gus that he was right—I am a grenade, and I will hurt him when I go.

grounded_facts: After crying and reflecting on her emotions, Hazel makes the decision to reach out to Gus by phone.
A private, emotionally charged moment in Hazel's backyard where she breaks down, calls Gus, and they confront the risks of their growing closeness.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting in the backyard, overwhelmed by everything—the sky, the old swing set my dad made, the sadness I carry—and I started crying. I didn’t want to be alone with it anymore, so I wiped my tears and decided to call Gus. When he answered, I told him how much I wanted to go to Amsterdam, how I didn’t want my life to end like this, and how the swing set was making me cry. He listened, and then he said he wanted to see that swing set of tears. We both looked at it, in silence, and I felt a little less alone. He finally said we had to do something about that stupid swing set, and I knew I’d let him in, even though I’m scared of what it means.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus collaboratively write a humorous Craigslist post about a swing set
memories.memory_text: I was sitting at the computer working on a funny Craigslist post about a swing set, and Gus stood beside me, helping out.

grounded_facts: Gus tells Hazel he likes her because she is uniquely herself, which marks a shift in emotional openness.
Gus compliments Hazel by explaining that her authentic self is what makes her special, strengthening emotional intimacy
memories.memory_text: Gus told me that he likes me because I'm so busy being myself that I don't even realize how utterly unprecedented I am, and I remember feeling like he really saw me.

grounded_facts: The swing set is delivered and loaded into the townie's pick-up truck, marking the completion of its installation at Hazel's house.
memories.memory_text: I watched as the townie finished loading the swing set into his pick-up truck, and I knew the delivery was finally complete at my house.

grounded_facts: Gus sneaks a quick kiss on Hazel's cheek, initiating a moment of intimacy that she responds to with mild disapproval.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus sneaking a quick kiss on my cheek, catching me off guard.

grounded_facts: In response to Gus's cheek kiss, Hazel playfully elbows him away, indicating mild protest with affectionate undertones.
memories.memory_text: I playfully elbowed him away in response, letting him know I wasn’t having it—but I didn’t really mean it.

grounded_facts: The moment immediately following the Support Group session, as Hazel and Isaac walk away from the gathering.
memories.memory_text: I walked with Isaac as we left the Support Group session together.

grounded_facts: Isaac asks Hazel whether she has romantic interest in someone previously discussed.
memories.memory_text: Isaac asked me if I liked him and whether I wanted to hook up, and I remember being surprised by the question.

grounded_facts: Hazel indicates that her feelings about a potential romantic connection are unclear and complex.
memories.memory_text: I told myself and Isaac that I don't know what I want, and that my feelings are complicated.

grounded_facts: Hazel reads an email from Lidewij Vliegenthart confirming the upcoming trip to Amsterdam, which she was not expecting.
memories.memory_text: I was reading an email from Lidewij Vliegenthart that said we were still going to Amsterdam with Augustus and my mom, which surprised me because I didn't expect it.

grounded_facts: Hazel urgently asks her mother if she informed the Genies that the trip was canceled, showing concern about miscommunication.
memories.memory_text: I urgently asked my mom if she had told the Genies the trip was canceled because I just got an email saying they still expected us, and I was worried there was a miscommunication.

grounded_facts: Frannie confirms to Hazel that the trip to Amsterdam is happening, after initially hesitating to disclose it.
memories.memory_text: I remember my mom finally telling me we're going to Amsterdam, after hesitating and saying she wasn't supposed to tell me until Dad got home.

grounded_facts: The coordinated effort to confirm and prepare for Hazel and family's trip to Amsterdam with Augustus Waters.
memories.memory_text: I realized there must have been some kind of coordinated effort to get the trip back on track, since my mom hadn't told me anything and Dr. Maria must have convinced her, but I wasn't sure exactly how it all came together.

grounded_facts: Hazel yells 'I LOVE YOU SO MUCH' and attempts to hug her mother after learning the trip is confirmed.
memories.memory_text: I yelled 'I LOVE YOU SO MUCH!' and tried to hug my mom when I heard the news, and she came over to me so we could embrace.

grounded_facts: Hazel texts Augustus to confirm his availability on May 3, signaling her renewed hope and excitement about the trip.
Hazel sends a text to Gus asking if he is free on May 3, using a cheerful tone with a smiley face.
memories.memory_text: I texted Gus to ask if he was still free on May 3, adding a smiley to keep it light, and when he replied with 'EVERYTHING'S COMING UP WATERS!', I couldn't help but smile—I felt a real spark of hope that the trip might actually happen.

grounded_facts: Hazel whispers a personal plea to her lungs, asking them to remain stable for one more week to allow the trip to happen.
memories.memory_text: I whispered to my lungs, asking them to hold it together just one more week, because I really needed them to cooperate if I was going to make this trip work.

grounded_facts: The family prepares to leave for Amsterdam, with luggage and medical equipment ready by the door.
memories.memory_text: I saw our luggage by the door, including my oxygen tank, and felt the buzz of excitement as I joined Frannie in the kitchen, knowing we were really about to leave for Amsterdam.

grounded_facts: A planned family trip to Amsterdam, marked by preparation and shared excitement.
memories.memory_text: I remember how we were all together in the kitchen, fully ready for the trip to Amsterdam, and how the air was charged with our shared enthusiasm as we prepared to depart.

grounded_facts: Hazel initiates the verbal expression of excitement by saying 'Amsterdam!', which is immediately echoed by Frannie and Michael, creating a moment of emotional synchrony.
Hazel, Frannie, and Michael each exclaim 'Amsterdam!' in sequence, showing shared enthusiasm for the trip.
memories.memory_text: I shouted 'Amsterdam!' first, and then Frannie and Michael echoed me, and in that moment I felt perfectly in sync with them, all of us caught up in the same burst of joy.

grounded_facts: Michael whispers to Hazel that he loves her and is proud of her, delivering an emotionally significant message.
memories.memory_text: He whispered to me that he loves me and is proud of me, so softly it felt like a secret just for me.

grounded_facts: Michael emotionally tells Hazel he is proud of her and loves her, showing deep paternal affection during their farewell.
memories.memory_text: I remember Michael holding me and saying he loves me and is proud of me—his voice was full of emotion, and I could feel how much he meant it.

grounded_facts: Unable to contain his emotions, Michael pulls Hazel into another hug after briefly letting go.
memories.memory_text: After he let go, he looked at me and just couldn’t stay away—he pulled me into another hug, and I laughed because it was so sweet.

grounded_facts: A family farewell occurring outside the house as Michael prepares to leave, involving emotional goodbyes with his wife and Hazel.
memories.memory_text: I remember standing outside the house, watching him finish packing the car and kiss his wife goodbye before coming over to me.

grounded_facts: Michael initiates a hug with Hazel, which she reciprocates, expressing emotional closeness.
memories.memory_text: He reached out and hugged me first, and I hugged him back—our embrace said everything words couldn’t.

memories.memory_text: I heard the airport announce pre-boarding for Flight 144 to Amsterdam, calling for passengers who need extra assistance, and I realized it was meant for me and Gus.

grounded_facts: A commercial airplane journey with Hazel, Gus, and Frannie aboard, involving takeoff, mid-flight movie watching, and landing.
memories.memory_text: I sat between Frannie and Gus on the plane, and I remember feeling his hand squeeze mine during takeoff; later, we watched a movie together while Frannie slept, and I found myself watching him more than the screen.

grounded_facts: During the flight, Hazel observes Gus watching a movie and realizes she is falling in love with him.
memories.memory_text: I watched Gus as he got caught up in the movie, his face lit by the screen, and I realized I was falling in love with him.

memories.memory_text: I heard the cab driver make a sarcastic comment about how Indiana is named after the Indians while they stole everything from them.

grounded_facts: Hazel questions whether the current location is truly Amsterdam, prompting the driver's explanation of the city's structure.

memories.memory_text: I rode in the back of a yellow cab with Gus and Frannie, and as we moved from the industrial outskirts into the city, I saw colorful row houses, houseboats, and bicycles along a canal, which left me astounded.

grounded_facts: Gus tells Hazel he will be nearby, offering comfort and support.

memories.memory_text: I remember arriving at the hotel room with Frannie, and Gus helping us bring our stuff inside before I sat down on the bed, already so tired.

memories.memory_text: I remember my mom telling me she’d do 'crazy Mom stuff' that night so I could have freedom for my date with Gus.

memories.memory_text: I sarcastically asked my mom if it was really okay with her that I'd be running around a foreign city known for vice with an older boy, just to see how she'd respond.

memories.memory_text: I saw that my mom avoided answering my question and instead got excited about getting me dressed, like changing the subject was easier than talking about what I really wanted to know.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Hazel and Gus ride together on a tram through Amsterdam at night, observing the cityscape and beginning their evening.

memories.memory_text: I shared with Gus that I had bought a 'death suit' for my 15th birthday, and he opened up about losing his leg and the fear he felt during treatment—we both let each other see the hard truths we carry.

memories.memory_text: I was in the hotel room with Frannie, getting ready to meet Van Houten, and she commented on my shirt by saying, "This is not a pipe."

grounded_facts: A planned meeting between Gus, Hazel, and author Peter Van Houten, which begins with tension and hostility.

I realized then that this meeting wasn’t going to go the way we hoped.

memories.memory_text: I saw the door open and Lidewij push Van Houten back, and then Gus and I exchanged a glance before stepping inside together.

memories.memory_text: I remember Gus and I arriving at Van Houten's house, being led into a sterile living room where we sat down to talk with him about his book.

grounded_facts: Shocked and hurt by Van Houten's cruelty, Lidewij declares she is resigning as his assistant.

memories.memory_text: I confronted Van Houten, demanding he tell me what happens to his characters after the novel ends, because I felt he owed us that answer.

memories.memory_text: I heard Van Houten say that the characters in his novel cease to exist after the story ends, and he refused to tell me what happens to them, insisting they are just fictions.

memories.memory_text: I told Van Houten to go fuck himself when he had the nerve to ask why I cared so much about my questions, and I meant it—when he shut the door without another word, I finally broke down.

grounded_facts: A planned encounter between Hazel, Gus, and author Peter Van Houten, intended to seek answers about his novel, which ends in emotional disappointment.
memories.memory_text: I was there with Gus to get answers from Van Houten, but the whole thing ended in disappointment the moment he closed the door on us.

grounded_facts: Gus reassures Hazel that their trip was not wasted on Van Houten but was instead an experience they shared.
memories.memory_text: Gus told me our trip wasn't wasted on Van Houten, but was instead something we shared, and I remember how he said it like it was enough.

grounded_facts: Hazel expresses guilt over spending her Wish on Van Houten, but Gus reframes it as an experience shared between them.
memories.memory_text: I felt guilty telling Gus that I spent his Wish on that asshole, but he told me I didn't spend it on Van Houten—I spent it on us.

memories.memory_text: I heard Lidewij apologize for Van Houten, saying she was sorry he was cruel and that she had hoped meeting us would help him, but it didn't.

memories.memory_text: I saw Gus stand firm and say he wouldn't go anywhere with Van Houten, making it clear he wouldn't take part in anything connected to that man ever again.

memories.memory_text: I refused to let my disability stop me—I told everyone I could climb those stairs, and I meant it, because I wasn't going to accept another disappointment.

memories.memory_text: I was part of a group visit to the Anne Frank House, and I remember Lidewij coming back from the ticket kiosk with news that affected us all—we were going inside despite the challenges.

memories.memory_text: I heard Lidewij tell us about how the bookcase hid the Frank family and others, sharing both facts and emotion as we stood there together.

memories.memory_text: I pushed myself to climb the narrow, steep stairs to the final hiding room, feeling every labored breath and the growing difficulty, and though I stumbled near the top, I pulled myself through and collapsed on the floor, exhausted but determined.

grounded_facts: Gus comforts Hazel as she struggles to breathe, affirming her strength.
memories.memory_text: When I struggled to breathe during the climb, Gus came to my side, wiped my brow, crouched beside me, and told me I was a champion.

grounded_facts: A guided visit to the historical hiding place of Anne Frank and her family, attended by Hazel, Gus, Lidewij, and other travelers.
memories.memory_text: I stood with Gus and Lidewij as part of a group of travelers beginning the tour of the historical hiding place, and I heard Lidewij explain that the bookcase had hidden Anne Frank's family and others.

grounded_facts: After watching the video about Anne Frank's final days, Hazel kisses Gus in a deeply emotional and intense moment, affirming their bond.
memories.memory_text: I kissed Gus after watching the video about Anne Frank's last days, and it was the most intense, passionate kiss I'd ever imagined, like it was just me and him against the world.

memories.memory_text: After we kissed, I noticed the travelers staring at us, and then they started clapping—someone even shouted 'bravo!'—and I realized how moved they were by us.

grounded_facts: Hazel responds to Gus's nervous revelation about his leg by telling him to stop being self-conscious, showing acceptance.
memories.memory_text: I told Gus to get over himself when he got self-conscious about his leg, because I accept him just as he is.

memories.memory_text: I was kissing Gus on his bed, and he tried to take my shirt off, but it got tangled in my oxygen tube—he couldn't figure it out, and we just ended up laughing together.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus verbally confess their love for each other during an intimate moment.
memories.memory_text: I told Augustus that I love him, and he said it back to me, and in that moment, I knew I was truly in love with him.

grounded_facts: Hazel, Gus, and Frannie meet at an outdoor cafe during the day, drinking coffee and discussing recent events.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting with Gus and Frannie at an outdoor cafe, drinking coffee in the sun and talking about what had happened recently.

memories.memory_text: I re-enacted the argument I had with Gus where I told him to get up, and he refused, saying 'Standing is for fools!'—we both giggled at how ridiculous it was.

grounded_facts: Hazel thinks she sees a brief eye contact between Gus and Frannie as Frannie leaves the table.
memories.memory_text: As she stood up, I thought I saw a brief moment of eye contact between Gus and Frannie, just for a second.

memories.memory_text: I was walking with Gus in Amsterdam when he said he needed to tell me something, and I could tell he was struggling—then I grabbed his arm and held on tight when he broke the news.

memories.memory_text: I hugged Augustus as tightly as I could and told him I was so sorry after he told me about his cancer, just wanting to comfort him in that moment.

memories.memory_text: I remember Augustus saying that the world is not a wish-granting factory, reflecting on how unfair life can be.

memories.memory_text: I told Gus I'm very fond of him, because I needed him to know how I felt after everything.

memories.memory_text: I was told that Gus suggests kissing Hazel in the moment, seeking connection and normalcy amid emotional pain.

memories.memory_text: I remember that In response to Gus's question, Hazel kisses him passionately without speaking.

memories.memory_text: I rested my head on Gus's shoulder during the flight, just letting myself be close to him.
