memories.memory_text: I felt the plane pull away from Amsterdam, and I knew our trip was really over.

grounded_facts: A planned meeting at the Indianapolis Airport baggage claim where Michael reunites with his wife, Hazel, and Gus after their return.
Michael sees Hazel, her mother, and Gus arriving at the baggage claim and emotionally welcomes them, hugging each family member including Gus.
memories.memory_text: I saw Michael waiting for me at the baggage claim with a sign that said 'My Beautiful Family (and Gus)' and he hugged me tightly when we met, kissing my mom and embracing Gus too.

grounded_facts: Gus attempts to shake Michael's hand, but Michael instead embraces him in a hug, indicating acceptance and affection.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gus try to shake Michael's hand, but Michael pulled him into a hug instead, which made me feel like he truly accepted him as part of our family.

grounded_facts: Hazel discloses that Gus has had a cancer recurrence, and Michael reveals he already knew from Mrs. Waters.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Hazel discloses that Gus has had a cancer recurrence, and Michael reveals he already knew from Mrs. Waters.

grounded_facts: A private, emotionally charged conversation between Hazel and her father about Gus's illness and adult uncertainty
memories.memory_text: I remember that A private, emotionally charged conversation between Hazel and her father about Gus's illness and adult uncertainty

grounded_facts: Hazel asks why Michael isn't offering the usual platitude, prompting him to express doubt
memories.memory_text: I asked Michael why he wasn't going to say the usual platitude like 'everything happens for a reason,' and he just responded with 'What's that?' before I pressed him on it.

grounded_facts: Michael admits he does not have the answers he expected to have as an adult, especially about meaning in suffering.
memories.memory_text: I heard Michael admit that he doesn't know the answers he thought he'd have as an adult, especially about meaning in suffering—he said knowing what you believe was supposed to come with being grown up, but that hasn't been his experience.

grounded_facts: When Isaac accidentally touches Gus's thigh, Gus jokingly says 'Whoa, I'm taken,' deflecting physical contact with humor.
memories.memory_text: I saw Isaac accidentally touch Gus's thigh, and Gus joked, 'Whoa, I'm taken,' which made me smile because it was so him.

grounded_facts: Isaac jokingly asks Hazel if she has written Gus's eulogy yet, unintentionally revealing Gus's unspoken wish.
memories.memory_text: Isaac asked me if I'd written Gus's eulogy yet, and I remember being surprised because it revealed something Gus hadn't directly told me at the time.

grounded_facts: A future event where Gus envisions having speakers, especially Hazel, deliver eulogies.
Gus asks Hazel to write a eulogy for his funeral, specifying that he wants her to be the primary speaker.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus telling me he wanted speakers at his funeral, especially me, and then formally asking if I would be kind enough to write something — I felt honored and said yes.

grounded_facts: Hazel lightly hits Isaac on the arm after he makes a teasing comment about her and Gus being adorable.
memories.memory_text: I lightly slapped Isaac on the arm after he said Gus and I were adorable, just to playfully shut him up.

grounded_facts: Isaac mentions a new girl in Support Group, indicating he is trying to move forward emotionally.
memories.memory_text: I heard Isaac say he was moving on, mentioning a new girl in Support Group, and I wondered how he could know such specific things about her.

grounded_facts: Isaac discloses that Monica has not contacted him since their breakup, not even to check on his health.
memories.memory_text: I asked Isaac if Monica had even checked on how he was doing, and I couldn't believe she hadn't reached out to him at all after their breakup.

grounded_facts: Hazel comes back to the car carrying a carton of eggs, indicating she has obtained them from an off-screen location.
memories.memory_text: I came back to the car holding a carton of eggs, letting Gus know I'd gotten them.

grounded_facts: Isaac begins throwing eggs at Monica's car under Gus's guidance, marking the start of a symbolic act of revenge.
Gus verbally directs Isaac, who is blind, to adjust his aim while throwing eggs.
memories.memory_text: I watched as Gus helped Isaac aim the eggs at Monica's car, telling him to adjust his throw, and I saw the first one miss completely.

grounded_facts: One of Isaac's eggs strikes the car door directly, setting off the alarm.
memories.memory_text: I saw one of Isaac's eggs hit the car door dead on, and the alarm went off right away.

grounded_facts: A group act of symbolic revenge where Hazel, Gus, and Isaac throw eggs at Monica's car.
memories.memory_text: I was part of throwing eggs at Monica's car with Gus and Isaac, and I remember gently kissing Gus on the cheek during it.

grounded_facts: Hazel expresses affection for Gus by kissing him on the cheek during the event.
Hazel kisses Gus on the cheek as a gesture of affection and admiration.
memories.memory_text: I kissed Gus on the cheek to show him how much I care and admire him.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Waters informs Hazel that Gus's chemotherapy will be stopped, conveying the gravity of his condition.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Mrs. Waters that they were going to stop Gus's chemotherapy, and I knew then how serious his condition had become.

grounded_facts: The medical team has decided to stop Gus's chemotherapy, indicating a worsening of his condition and a shift in treatment approach.
memories.memory_text: I was told they're going to stop Gus's chemotherapy, which means his condition has gotten worse and they're changing how they're treating him.

grounded_facts: Hazel asks if she can visit Gus, showing her desire to be with him.
memories.memory_text: I asked if I could see him, because I just wanted to be with Gus one more time.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Waters tells Hazel they must 'be a family now,' subtly excluding her and reinforcing familial privilege in the final moments.
memories.memory_text: I heard Mrs. Waters say they had to be a family now, and I understood she meant I didn't belong in that space with them.

grounded_facts: Hazel chooses to stay in the waiting room, sitting in the same chair Gus once occupied while waiting for her, symbolizing a role reversal and emotional continuity.
memories.memory_text: I chose to stay in the waiting room and sat in the same chair Gus once sat in while waiting for me, feeling how we’d switched places.

grounded_facts: A visit by Hazel to the hospital where Gus is being treated, resulting in a significant emotional exchange with his mother.
memories.memory_text: I remember rushing into the hospital and hugging Mrs. Waters, sitting with her as she started to cry, and later watching her walk back to Gus's room after we hugged again—I stayed behind, sitting in the same chair Gus once waited in for me, feeling how much had changed.

grounded_facts: Hazel expresses anger and frustration toward Gus's preoccupation with being remembered, challenging his belief that a meaningful life requires widespread recognition.
Hazel angrily confronts Gus for prioritizing legacy over the love and life they share, asserting that her remembrance and affection should be enough.
memories.memory_text: I stood up, my anger rising as I confronted Gus about his obsession with being remembered, telling him that I think he's special and that my love and remembrance should be enough — that this life with me and our people isn't nothing, and I just wished he could be happy with that.

grounded_facts: A second picnic between Hazel and Gus at the Indianapolis Museum of Art, featuring champagne in Winnie the Pooh cups, set on a hill overlooking the 'Funky Bones' art installation.
memories.memory_text: I pushed Gus in his wheelchair to our spot on the hill overlooking the 'Funky Bones' art installation, and we had a picnic with champagne poured into Winnie the Pooh cups, trying to keep things light even though it was hard.

grounded_facts: After Hazel's emotional outburst, Gus abandons his fixation on posthumous fame and accepts the significance of personal love and connection.
memories.memory_text: I could see Gus was still holding on to that dream of being famous after he died, but when I told him that I’d remember him and love him, he finally seemed to understand that what we have is enough.

grounded_facts: Gus acknowledges Hazel is right, apologizes, and toasts to their life together, signaling emotional reconnection.
memories.memory_text: I remember how he looked at me and said, 'You're right,' then apologized and raised his cup to toast our life together—I felt us reconnect in that moment.

grounded_facts: Gus calls Hazel late at night from a gas station, indicating something is wrong and asking for her help.
Gus, sounding weak, calls Hazel and asks her to come help him at the gas station because something is wrong.
A phone call initiated by Gus to Hazel at 2:35am, breaking normal communication patterns and signaling emergency.
memories.memory_text: I was startled when my phone buzzed at 2:35am—it was Gus calling, and I knew something was wrong. He sounded weak and said he was at the gas station, asking me to come help him right away.

grounded_facts: Hazel locates Gus alone in his car at the Speedway gas station, discovering him in critical condition with a visibly infected G-tube site and high fever.
memories.memory_text: I drove to the Speedway gas station and found Gus alone in his car, his shirt stained with blood and vomit; when I saw the tube leaking from his belly and lifted his shirt to find his abdomen bright red, I touched his forehead and realized he was burning up with fever.

grounded_facts: Gus desperately begs Hazel not to call emergency services, expressing that he will never forgive her if she does.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus begging me not to call 911, his voice breaking as he said he'd never forgive me if I did.

grounded_facts: Despite Gus's desperate pleas not to, Hazel decides to call emergency services, marking a turning point in his loss of control over his final moments.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't fix it myself, so I made the call—I got out my phone and dialed 911 even though he was pleading with me not to.

grounded_facts: Gus sits alone in his car at a gas station, physically deteriorated and emotionally broken, after attempting a small act of independence by buying cigarettes.
memories.memory_text: I saw how weak Gus was—barely able to speak, throwing up without the strength to turn away, and then breaking down in tears—and I realized he had come here trying to do something small on his own, but his body had failed him completely.

grounded_facts: Emergency medical technicians respond to a call and transport Gus to the hospital after Hazel dials 911.
memories.memory_text: I called 911 because I knew I couldn’t help him alone, and I watched as the EMTs arrived and loaded him into the ambulance for emergency transport to the hospital.

grounded_facts: EMTs transport Gus to the hospital in an ambulance, with Hazel permitted to ride along, signifying the end of his autonomous outing.
memories.memory_text: I saw the EMTs load Gus into the ambulance, and I was allowed to ride with him in the back, which meant I could stay by his side as we left the scene.

grounded_facts: Hazel rides with Gus in the ambulance as he drifts in and out of consciousness, during which he requests poetry and she composes a personal verse for him.
memories.memory_text: I rode with Gus in the ambulance, holding his hand as he drifted in and out of consciousness; when he asked me to read him something, I recited a poem and then made up my own, whispering 'So much depends upon this observer of the universe' as I cradled his head.

grounded_facts: Hazel reads and then improvises a poem for Gus in the ambulance to soothe him as he fades in and out of consciousness.
To comfort Gus during the ambulance ride, Hazel improvises a poetic variation on 'The Red Wheelbarrow,' personalizing it to his condition and their moment.
memories.memory_text: I read 'The Red Wheelbarrow' to Gus and then improvised my own version, saying 'so much depends upon this observer of the universe,' because I wanted to comfort him as he drifted in and out, holding his head in my arms.

grounded_facts: Hazel supports Gus physically as he enters the house after returning from the hospital.
memories.memory_text: I helped support Gus as we got him inside the house after he came back from the hospital.

grounded_facts: Gus comes back to his house after being discharged from the hospital, physically unwell but alive.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gus come home from the hospital; he didn't look good, but he was alive, and I was there to help get him inside.

grounded_facts: Gus no longer sleeps in his basement or his own bed; he now sleeps in a hospital bed set up in a guest room.
memories.memory_text: I noticed that Gus no longer sleeps in his basement or his own bed; now he's in a hospital bed set up in the guest room.

grounded_facts: Gus and Hazel are spending time together watching sports on television in the guest room.
memories.memory_text: I was with Gus in the guest room, and we spent time together watching sports on television.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus spend time together on the porch, seeking fresh air in a quiet moment.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting with Gus on the porch, just reading my book while he sat quietly, both of us taking in the fresh air during a quiet moment.

grounded_facts: Hazel waves to get Gus's attention, initiating connection.
memories.memory_text: I waved to Gus to get his attention because I wanted to reconnect with him when he seemed distant.

grounded_facts: Gus appears to wake from a dreamlike or dissociative state upon Hazel waving to him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Gus look over at me as if he was waking from a dream after I waved, like he wasn't really there before.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus share a moment of mutual, fragile positivity through smiling.
memories.memory_text: I managed to smile at Gus, and I saw him manage one back, and for a moment we shared something fragile but real between us.

grounded_facts: Gus calls Hazel and asks her to meet him at the Literal Heart of Jesus in 20 minutes, reaffirming his love before ending the call.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Gus calls Hazel and asks her to meet him at the Literal Heart of Jesus in 20 minutes, reaffirming his love before ending the call.

grounded_facts: During an argument about eating, Hazel breaks down and declares that she is dying and will leave her parents alone, expressing fear and helplessness.
memories.memory_text: I broke down and told my mom I can't stay healthy because I'm dying, and I'm going to leave her alone, and she won't be a mother anymore, and I just couldn't hold it in anymore.

grounded_facts: Frannie tells Hazel that she will always be her mother, even after death, offering comfort and continuity.
memories.memory_text: I remember my mom telling me that she will always be my mother, even after I die, and that as long as either of us is alive, she’ll still be my mom.

grounded_facts: In a moment of distress, Hazel tells her mother she will be relieved when Hazel dies and no longer needs care.
memories.memory_text: I told my mom I worry she won't have a life after I die, that she'll just sit around staring at the walls or worse, because I won't be there for her to care for.

grounded_facts: Frannie discloses that she is taking online classes toward a master's in social work, indicating plans for a future beyond Hazel's illness.
memories.memory_text: I remember when Mom told me she was taking online classes to get her master's in social work.

grounded_facts: Hazel reacts with joy and pride upon learning her mother is pursuing a master's in social work.
memories.memory_text: I felt so proud and happy when I heard about Mom's plans that I hugged her and told her, 'This is awesome! This is fantastic! I'm so excited! You're gonna be so great, Mom!'

grounded_facts: A family dinner during which Hazel receives a call from Gus, leading to emotional confrontation and reconciliation about her illness and future.
memories.memory_text: I remember that A family dinner during which Hazel receives a call from Gus, leading to emotional confrontation and reconciliation about her illness and future.

grounded_facts: After emotional reconciliation, Hazel agrees to eat later, signaling renewed willingness to care for herself.
memories.memory_text: I remember breaking down and telling Mom I couldn't stay healthy because I'm dying, and how she insisted she'd always be my mother. I worried she wouldn't have a life without me, but when she told me about her plans, I felt proud and promised I’d eat later before rushing off to meet Gus.

grounded_facts: Gus directly asks Hazel to speak at his funeral, establishing emotional intimacy and trust.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus asking me directly if I would speak at his funeral, and it made me feel how much he trusted me.

grounded_facts: Gus arranges a pre-funeral event in the Literal Heart of Jesus room, inviting Hazel and Isaac to participate in a mock funeral while he is still alive.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Gus that he arranged a pre-funeral event in the Literal Heart of Jesus room while he was still alive, and he invited me and Isaac to be part of it.

grounded_facts: Isaac delivers a mock eulogy for Gus, blending humor, criticism, and deep affection, culminating in a declaration of how Gus changed his view of the world.
memories.memory_text: I listened to Isaac's eulogy for Gus, hearing him call Augustus a self-aggrandizing bastard but also say he’d turn down robot eyes because he doesn’t want to see a world without him, and I could hear the pain and love in his voice.

grounded_facts: After Isaac finishes his speech and becomes emotional, Hazel remembers he is blind and helps him back to his seat.
memories.memory_text: After Isaac finished speaking and started to break down, I remembered he couldn’t see, and when he asked for my help, I got up and walked him back to his seat.

grounded_facts: Hazel delivers an emotional eulogy for Gus, expressing gratitude for their 'little infinity' and framing their love through the metaphor of unequal infinities.
memories.memory_text: I stood at the dais with my notes, trying to hold myself together as I spoke about Augustus Waters, the great star-crossed love of my life. I wanted to tell our epic love story, but I knew it would vanish with me—so instead, I told them about math. I remembered how some infinities are bigger than others, and I told Gus how thankful I was for our little infinity, because he gave me a forever within the numbered days we had.

grounded_facts: A self-organized mock funeral held by Gus while still alive, taking place in a church room, where friends deliver eulogies and reflect on his life.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the mock funeral Gus organized in the church room, where I sat beside him and later delivered a eulogy about our love and how some infinities are bigger than others.

grounded_facts: A late-night phone call delivers the news of Augustus Waters' death to Hazel.
Hazel receives a phone call in the middle of the night that confirms Augustus Waters has died.
memories.memory_text: I woke up to the phone ringing at 4am, and I knew something was wrong—I answered it and learned that Augustus Waters had died.

grounded_facts: Hazel's parents enter her room and physically comfort her after she learns of Augustus's death.
Upon confirmation of Augustus's death, Hazel breaks down emotionally and is comforted by her parents.
memories.memory_text: I broke down when I heard the news, and I remember my parents rushing into my room and holding me tightly as I cried.

grounded_facts: Despite her efforts to numb her emotions with loud music, Hazel emotionally breaks down.
memories.memory_text: I sat in the car in the dark, blaring the loudest music I could to drown out the horrors, but it didn't protect me—I fell apart anyway.

grounded_facts: Hazel reveals in voiceover that she reserved her perfect score of ten for something significant, implying emotional significance behind her rating system.
memories.memory_text: I remember saying out loud to myself that I was saving my ten, because I wanted the perfect score to mean something truly meaningful.

grounded_facts: Hazel notices Peter Van Houten in the church during the funeral, which shocks and confuses her.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Peter Van Houten in the church during the funeral, and I was completely shocked and confused to see him there.

grounded_facts: The Waters parents open their arms to Hazel and tell her that Gus loved her very much.
memories.memory_text: When the Waters parents saw me, they opened their arms, and I went to them; they told me that Gus loved me very much, and I told them he loved them too.

grounded_facts: Hazel approaches the coffin, sees Augustus in his suit, breaks down momentarily, then composes herself and kisses his cheek.
memories.memory_text: I approached the coffin after hesitating, saw Augustus in the suit he wore to Oranjee, broke down for a moment, but then composed myself and kissed his cheek.

grounded_facts: Hazel secretly places a pack of Camel Lights between Augustus and the lining of the coffin as a personal tribute.
memories.memory_text: I looked around to make sure no one was watching, then I pulled out a pack of Camel Lights and slipped it between Augustus and the lining of the coffin as my private tribute.

grounded_facts: Van Houten whispers to Hazel, 'We need to fake pray now,' acknowledging the absurdity of the moment.
memories.memory_text: Van Houten leaned over and whispered to me, 'We need to fake pray now,' and I understood he was acknowledging how absurd the moment felt.

grounded_facts: Hazel gives a speech at the funeral, identifying herself as Gus's girlfriend and quoting a meaningful phrase from his home.
In response to being called a 'special friend,' Hazel publicly declares, 'I was his girlfriend.'
memories.memory_text: I stood at the podium and gave my speech, making sure everyone knew I was his girlfriend, not just a 'special friend,' and I quoted something meaningful from his home.

grounded_facts: Hazel arrives at the church with her parents and participates in the funeral service for Augustus Waters.
A formal funeral service held in a church for Augustus Waters, attended by family, friends, and mourners.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at the church with my parents and saw how full it was with mourners there for Augustus; I stood in the back and watched the service, hearing the speaker talk about Gus's courage while his parents nodded along, and I knew I had to face the coffin even though I wasn't sure I wanted to.

grounded_facts: A burial ceremony for Gus attended by friends, family, and Van Houten.
memories.memory_text: I watched the burial ceremony for Gus, surrounded by friends and family, but I kept my gaze turned away, lost in my own thoughts.

grounded_facts: Van Houten asks Hazel for a ride to the bottom of the hill.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Van Houten that he needed a ride, just to the bottom of the hill, as he approached me after the funeral.

grounded_facts: Van Houten discloses that he had a daughter who died of leukemia, revealing a personal connection to Anna's story.
Van Houten shares that his daughter died of leukemia, creating a moment of connection.
memories.memory_text: I learned that Van Houten had a daughter who died of leukemia, just like Anna, and that she suffered for a long time when she was eight.

grounded_facts: Van Houten expresses genuine remorse for his behavior and for causing pain to Hazel and Gus.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Van Houten that he was sorry for being rude to me and Gus, and for ruining our trip, and that he was trying to make things right.

grounded_facts: Hazel refuses Van Houten's written explanation and demands he leave her car.
Hazel refuses the explanation Van Houten offers in writing, crumples the paper, and demands he leave her car.
memories.memory_text: I refused the explanation Van Houten handed me, crumpled up his paper, threw it at him, and told him to get out of my car because I didn't care—he's a drunk and a jerk and I needed to go home and grieve.

grounded_facts: Hazel reluctantly agrees to give Van Houten a ride after the funeral, despite her initial resistance.
memories.memory_text: I reluctantly agreed to give Van Houten a ride, even though I wanted to be alone, and I let him out as soon as we reached the roadside.

grounded_facts: Hazel lies in front of the TV, emotionally overwhelmed, with tears falling uncontrollably while 'Top Model' plays.
memories.memory_text: I was lying in front of the TV watching 'Top Model,' but I wasn't really seeing it—I was lost in my own thoughts, and the tears just started falling without me being able to stop them.

grounded_facts: Hazel rises from her position in front of the TV, ending her passive state.
memories.memory_text: I got up from the floor, finally moving after just lying there, ending that heavy, still moment.

grounded_facts: Michael asks Hazel if he can come in after knocking on the bathroom door.
memories.memory_text: I heard Michael ask, 'Can I come in?' after he knocked on the bathroom door.

grounded_facts: Hazel unlocks the bathroom door to allow Michael to enter after he knocks.
memories.memory_text: I unlocked the bathroom door to let Michael in after he knocked.

grounded_facts: Michael acknowledges his grief but affirms that loving the deceased was a privilege, showing emotional resilience.
memories.memory_text: I saw how Michael acknowledged his grief but still said it was a privilege to love the deceased, and that showed me his strength.

grounded_facts: Michael tells Hazel that loving the deceased was a privilege, reinforcing emotional connection.
memories.memory_text: I remember Michael telling me that loving the deceased was a privilege, and it made me feel how much he values love.

grounded_facts: Michael physically comforts Hazel by letting her cry on his shoulder and holding her tightly, marking a shift in his emotional composure.
memories.memory_text: I sat on the bathroom floor crying, and Michael knelt down beside me, let me press my face into his shirt, and held me tightly while I cried—he didn't let go, and I nodded against him, feeling how much he cared.

grounded_facts: Michael implies that the love they felt for the deceased reflects how much they love Hazel.
memories.memory_text: I heard Michael say that the way they loved the deceased gives you an idea how they feel about me, and it made me feel deeply loved.

grounded_facts: Hazel gains emotional strength from Michael's composed presence and words.
memories.memory_text: I drew strength from Michael's calm presence and the way he spoke, helping me feel more grounded in that moment.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Isaac sit on Isaac's roof after entering through his bedroom window, engaging in a serious conversation about Gus's death and the letter.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Hazel and Isaac sit on Isaac's roof after entering through his bedroom window, engaging in a serious conversation about Gus's death and the letter.

grounded_facts: Hazel confirms she is very angry about Gus's death, sharing her grief with Isaac.
memories.memory_text: I told Isaac I was very angry about Gus's death when he asked me.

grounded_facts: Hazel discovers that the letter from Van Houten was actually written by Gus, which shocks her and prompts her to leave immediately.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Hazel discovers that the letter from Van Houten was actually written by Gus, which shocks her and prompts her to leave immediately.

grounded_facts: Upon learning the letter was written by Gus, Hazel decides to leave immediately.
memories.memory_text: When I heard the letter was from Gus, I was shocked—my heart started racing—and I knew I had to leave right away, so I told Isaac I needed to go.

grounded_facts: Hazel discovers a crumpled letter from Van Houten under the passenger seat of her car after searching frantically through trash.
memories.memory_text: I was searching frantically through the trash in my car, desperate to find what Van Houten had given me, and just as I was about to give up, I saw a crumpled letter beneath the passenger seat; I reached under, pulled it out, and unfolded it.

grounded_facts: Through the letter, Gus conveys that Hazel was loved deeply, not widely, and that she understood the truth about legacy and connection.
memories.memory_text: I learned from Gus's words that he believed I was loved deeply, not widely, and that I understood the truth about legacy and connection—that being loved by just one person completely is more meaningful than being admired by many.

grounded_facts: As Hazel reads the letter, Gus's voice narrates a eulogy he requested Van Houten to revise, expressing his love and understanding of Hazel's legacy.
memories.memory_text: As I read the letter, Gus's voice filled my mind, narrating his request to Van Houten to revise my eulogy, expressing his deep love and understanding of who I truly am.

grounded_facts: Gus asks Van Houten to revise Hazel's eulogy, proposing a collaboration based on their complementary strengths.
memories.memory_text: I realized Gus had asked Van Houten to revise my eulogy, combining his honesty with Van Houten's skill as a writer because he believed we'd make a good team—one a good person but a shitty writer, the other a shitty person but a good writer—and through this, he wanted to ensure my legacy was captured truthfully and beautifully.

grounded_facts: Gus holds Hazel's hand and mentally imagines a world without them, finding it worthless.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus holding my hand, and I could tell he was thinking deeply—like he was imagining a world without us, and how worthless that would be.

grounded_facts: Hazel goes to the backyard, lies on the grass, and gazes at the stars, mirroring the film's opening image.
memories.memory_text: I walked out to the backyard, lay down on the grass with my oxygen tank beside me, and looked up at the stars, just like at the beginning of the movie.

grounded_facts: Gus declares his deep love for Hazel and shares his belief that while pain is inevitable, one can choose who is allowed to cause it.
memories.memory_text: I remember Gus telling me how much he loved me, saying I was so beautiful and funny, and that even though you can't choose whether you get hurt, you can choose who gets to hurt you—I hope I made the right choice in letting him in.

grounded_facts: After hearing Gus's words, Hazel silently affirms her acceptance of their love and shared decisions by saying 'Ok' to the universe.
Hazel verbally affirms her readiness and acceptance by saying 'Ok' to the universe, echoing Gus's earlier question.
memories.memory_text: After hearing Gus's voice, I closed my eyes, held his letter to my chest, and when I opened them again, I said 'Ok' to the universe—answering him, accepting everything we had.
