grounded_facts: After bumping into each other, Gus and Hazel exchange brief, polite apologies.
memories.memory_text: After we collided, I said 'My bad. No, it's...' and she apologized too, so I know we both meant to be polite in that awkward moment.

grounded_facts: Hazel collides with Gus, a strikingly attractive boy, leading to a moment of mutual awareness and speechlessness.
memories.memory_text: I bumped into a girl as I was walking, and for a moment we just looked at each other—I could tell she noticed me, and I felt this sudden awareness between us, like something shifted.

grounded_facts: A gathering of cancer patients in a church basement for sharing experiences and emotional support.
memories.memory_text: I was in the church basement with the others, part of this cancer support group where we all come together to share our experiences and offer each other emotional support.

grounded_facts: Isaac reveals he will undergo another surgery soon and will likely become blind as a result.
memories.memory_text: I heard Isaac say he was going to have another surgery soon and that he’d likely be blind afterward, and he admitted it was going to suck even though he didn’t want to complain.

grounded_facts: Hazel meets Augustus's persistent stare with equal intensity, initiating a silent contest of wills.
memories.memory_text: I locked eyes with Hazel, holding my gaze steady because I wasn't going to look away first.

grounded_facts: Hazel initiates and wins a silent staring contest with Augustus after feeling his persistent gaze.
memories.memory_text: I think Hazel started the staring contest by meeting my stare, and I must've blinked first because she seemed to win it.

grounded_facts: Augustus reveals his name, age, and cancer history, including losing a leg to osteosarcoma and being in remission.
memories.memory_text: I introduced myself, telling them I'm Augustus Waters, 17 years old, and that I lost a leg to osteosarcoma about a year and a half ago but am now in remission.

grounded_facts: Augustus states that his greatest fear is oblivion, because he wants to live an extraordinary life and be remembered.
memories.memory_text: I shared that I want to live an extraordinary life and be remembered, and that my greatest fear is oblivion—failing to leave a lasting mark.

grounded_facts: Hazel argues that oblivion is inevitable for everyone, and that fearing it is pointless because even great historical figures will eventually be forgotten.
Hazel publicly responds to Augustus's fear of oblivion by arguing it is inevitable and should be ignored.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel telling me that oblivion is inevitable for everyone, even great figures like Cleopatra or Mozart, and that fearing it is pointless because no one remembers them forever anyway.

grounded_facts: A casual gathering outside the church after an event, where teens socialize and couples interact.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the other teens hanging out and socializing after the event, like Isaac and Monica being all over each other near her car.

grounded_facts: Hazel criticizes Augustus for holding a cigarette, seeing it as self-destructive and hypocritical given his cancer history.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Hazel thought I was being hypocritical and self-destructive by holding a cigarette, especially after surviving cancer.

grounded_facts: Augustus shocks Hazel by pulling out a cigarette but explains it is unlit and symbolic — representing control over one's fate despite danger.
memories.memory_text: I pulled out a cigarette in front of Hazel and saw her shock, so I explained it’s unlit and just a metaphor—putting the thing that could kill me between my teeth without ever giving it the power to do so.

grounded_facts: Hazel encounters Augustus (Gus) for the first time outside the church; he approaches her, compliments her, and initiates conversation that leads to a connection.
Augustus tells Hazel she is beautiful, marking the beginning of their romantic tension.
Augustus invites Hazel to watch a movie immediately, proposing an impromptu outing.
memories.memory_text: I approached Hazel, asked for her full name, told her she was beautiful because I meant it, and then suggested we watch a movie right then—just an impromptu idea to seize the moment.

grounded_facts: Hazel declines her mother's offer to go home, choosing instead to follow through on impromptu plans with Augustus.
memories.memory_text: I was told Hazel turned down her mom’s ride home because she’d made plans with me.

grounded_facts: Hazel reacts with sarcasm and dry humor to Gus's admission of being a bad driver.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel responding with sarcasm when I admitted my driving history, saying 'You don't say' and later 'I'm surprised you have a license,' her dry humor making me laugh despite the vulnerability.

grounded_facts: A car ride during which Hazel and Gus engage in personal conversation while traveling together.
memories.memory_text: I remember driving with Hazel and having a real conversation, opening up about my struggles with the test while she sat beside me, reacting with her dry wit.

grounded_facts: Gus admits to failing his driving test multiple times and jokes about his poor driving being a 'cancer perk.'
Gus discloses that he failed his driving test multiple times and barely passed on the fourth attempt, with an instructor deeming his driving 'unpleasant but not technically unsafe.'
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel I failed the driving test a couple of times and only passed on the fourth try, remembering how the instructor said my driving was 'unpleasant but not technically unsafe,' and I joked that getting my license was a total cancer perk.

grounded_facts: Hazel takes a deep breath and begins recounting the discovery of her cancer, signaling a moment of emotional significance.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel take a deep breath, and then she told me, 'I was 13 when they found it,' starting to share her story in a way that felt different and important.

grounded_facts: Hazel reveals that her tumors have shrunk and her metastases have barely progressed, indicating a temporary medical stabilization despite ongoing lung issues.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel telling me that her tumors had shrunk and her metastases had barely progressed, which gave me some hope even though her lungs were still fragile.

grounded_facts: An informal, intimate conversation between Hazel and Gus during a car ride, serving as emotional and informational bonding time.
memories.memory_text: I was driving the car with one eye on the road and the other on Hazel, and I remember feeling totally dazzled by her during that quiet, intimate conversation we had.

grounded_facts: Gus playfully attributes Hazel's sophistication to her being a college girl after learning she has her GED.
memories.memory_text: I called Hazel a college girl and said it explained her aura of sophistication, just to tease her a little.

grounded_facts: Hazel responds to Gus's joke with a light shove, signaling ease and growing intimacy.
memories.memory_text: I smiled at her after my joke, and she smiled back and gave me a light shove on the arm—I could feel us easing into each other.

grounded_facts: Gus successfully drives and parks his car in his driveway, marking the end of the car ride and transition to a new location.
memories.memory_text: I successfully drove us home and parked my car in the driveway, and I said, 'We're here,' marking the end of the ride and our arrival.

grounded_facts: Gus rolls his eyes when explaining his parents' engraved plaques as 'encouragements', signaling mild embarrassment or affectionate mockery to Hazel.
memories.memory_text: I rolled my eyes when I told Hazel about my parents' engraved plaques being called 'encouragements,' not taking it too seriously.

grounded_facts: Gus's parents are preparing dinner in the kitchen when Hazel arrives with Gus.
memories.memory_text: I saw my parents in the kitchen getting dinner ready when Hazel came over with me.

grounded_facts: Hazel clarifies that she goes by 'Hazel', not 'Hazel Grace', asserting her preferred identity.
memories.memory_text: I heard Hazel say her name was just 'Hazel,' not 'Hazel Grace,' when I introduced her to my parents.

grounded_facts: Gus brings Hazel into his house and introduces her to his parents, who are making dinner in the kitchen.
memories.memory_text: I brought Hazel into my house and introduced her to my parents while they were making dinner in the kitchen.

grounded_facts: Gus abruptly ends the parental introduction and pulls Hazel downstairs, redirecting focus to private time together.
memories.memory_text: I abruptly told my parents we were going downstairs and then pulled Hazel with me to my bedroom, wanting some privacy.

grounded_facts: Gus leads Hazel downstairs to his basement bedroom, revealing personal space filled with video games, band posters, and basketball memorabilia.
memories.memory_text: I led Hazel down to my basement bedroom, showing her around my space with the video games, band posters, and all my basketball stuff—I could tell she was taking it in.

grounded_facts: Hazel struggles with breathing after descending stairs and standing, requiring rest on Gus's bed.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel struggling to breathe after we got downstairs, so I stayed close when she sat on my bed and said she might faint—I waited with her until her breathing slowed down.

grounded_facts: Hazel names 'An Imperial Affliction' as her favorite novel, describing it as deeply meaningful and spiritually significant to her.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel telling me that her favorite novel was 'An Imperial Affliction,' and she called it her bible—something deeply meaningful that helped her make sense of being sick.

grounded_facts: Their hands briefly tangle when exchanging books, creating a moment of romantic tension and connection.
memories.memory_text: When I handed her the book, our hands got tangled for a brief moment, and I felt this sudden, quiet spark between us.

grounded_facts: Gus gives Hazel a novelization of his favorite video game in exchange for her reading 'An Imperial Affliction', forming a symbolic pact.
Gus commits to reading 'An Imperial Affliction' despite initial skepticism, marking a shift in his attitude toward Hazel's inner world.
memories.memory_text: I gave her the novelization of my favorite video game and promised to read 'An Imperial Affliction' even though I wasn't sure I'd like it, making a kind of pact between us.

grounded_facts: Gus flirts with Hazel by saying he loves it when she talks medical, responding to her explanation of cold hands.
memories.memory_text: I flirted with her by saying I love it when she talks medical, after she explained why her hands were cold.

grounded_facts: Gus and Hazel have an intimate conversation in his basement bedroom after being introduced to his parents.
memories.memory_text: I sat with Hazel on my bed in the basement, asked her about her story, and we ended up talking deeply about her favorite book and even flirted a little.

grounded_facts: Hazel is reading a novella written by Gus, indicating he gave her the book, which represents a personal and creative gesture.
memories.memory_text: I think I gave Hazel the novella, and her reading it might mean she values what I wrote, though I'm not sure how much it really means to her.

grounded_facts: Hazel reads Gus's novella in bed at night while Frannie briefly visits the room.
memories.memory_text: I was reading my novella in bed one night when Frannie came into the room for a moment.

grounded_facts: Hazel insists she is not waiting for Gus to call, despite clear signs of anticipation.
memories.memory_text: I told my mom I wasn't waiting for Gus to call, even though I knew I was hoping he would.

grounded_facts: Hazel repeatedly checks her phone while engaging in daily activities, revealing her emotional preoccupation with hearing from Gus.
memories.memory_text: I kept checking my phone while brushing my teeth, watching TV, eating breakfast, and staring out the window, trying to pretend I didn't care if Gus called.

grounded_facts: A family dinner at Hazel's home where Hazel receives texts from Gus.
memories.memory_text: I remember sending Hazel a series of frantic texts during what I assumed was her family dinner, asking her if her copy of the book ended mid-sentence too, because I couldn’t believe mine did — it felt like a violation of everything books are supposed to be.

grounded_facts: Hazel receives a series of texts from Gus about his frustration with a book ending mid-sentence, which visibly affects her mood.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel how upset I was that the book ended in the middle of a sentence, yelling through texts that it couldn’t possibly be real, and I could imagine her reacting — I hoped it made her smile, even if I was genuinely distressed at the time.

grounded_facts: Hazel initiates a phone call to Gus, who answers immediately.
memories.memory_text: I answered Hazel's call right away when she rang me.

grounded_facts: During the call, a loud wail is heard from Gus's end, indicating possible emotional or physical distress.
memories.memory_text: I let out a loud wail during the call, and I know Hazel heard it.

grounded_facts: A phone call initiated by Hazel and received by Gus, beginning with casual banter and interrupted by a sudden emotional outburst.
memories.memory_text: Hazel and I were joking around on the phone when something inside me just broke and I couldn't hold it back.

grounded_facts: After hearing a wail from Gus's end of the line, Hazel immediately checks if he is okay.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Hazel asked if I was okay after she heard me wail on the phone.

grounded_facts: Isaac experiences a severe emotional collapse, wailing uncontrollably on Gus's couch.
memories.memory_text: I saw Isaac buried in my couch, wailing uncontrollably like a banshee during a nervous breakdown.

grounded_facts: Gus rhetorically asks Hazel whether her presence or association with the support group would improve or worsen Isaac's state.
memories.memory_text: I asked Hazel whether her being there or being tied to the support group would make Isaac's state better or worse, not knowing which it would be.

grounded_facts: Gus attempts to stabilize the situation by commanding Isaac to focus on him.
memories.memory_text: I tried to stabilize things by telling Isaac, 'Focus. On. Me,' trying to pull him back by directing his attention.

grounded_facts: Gus decides to involve Hazel and asks her how quickly she can arrive at his location.
memories.memory_text: I decided to call Hazel and asked her how fast she could get here, needing her help with Isaac's crisis.

grounded_facts: Hazel physically and verbally supports Isaac after he reveals his heartbreak.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel ask Isaac if he wanted to talk about it, and then I watched her rub his shoulder in sympathy as he cried.

grounded_facts: Isaac discloses that Monica ended their relationship, unable to cope with his impending blindness, marking a key emotional turning point in the scene.
memories.memory_text: I heard Isaac say that Monica ended things because she couldn't handle his impending blindness, and that she wouldn't say 'always' back to him, like he was already gone.

grounded_facts: Gus quotes a line from Hazel's favorite book, leading to mutual recognition and emotional connection.
memories.memory_text: I quoted 'Pain demands to be felt' from Hazel's favorite book, and I saw her light up when she realized I was quoting it—she beamed because I totally get the book, and that's when I knew we had a real connection.

grounded_facts: Gus reveals his deep engagement with 'An Imperial Affliction' and his wish to contact its reclusive author, Peter Van Houten, initiating a shared intellectual bond with Hazel.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel how the ending of 'An Imperial Affliction' feels like a violation of the contract between author and reader, and I asked her if she'd ever tried contacting Peter Van Houten, because I really want to know what happens after the story cuts off.

grounded_facts: Gus hands Isaac a trophy and nods, giving him implicit permission to break it as a form of emotional release.
memories.memory_text: I handed Isaac one of my basketball trophies, and when he looked at me like he needed permission, I let him know it was okay—he went ahead and smashed it to pieces.

grounded_facts: With Gus's encouragement, Isaac transitions from passive grief to physical release by destroying Gus's basketball trophies, symbolizing emotional catharsis.
memories.memory_text: I encouraged Isaac to keep going, telling him to go to town, and I watched as he grabbed more of my trophies and smashed them, helping him release his pain while Hazel and I took it in.

grounded_facts: An informal support gathering in Gus's basement where Hazel visits Isaac during his emotional crisis following a breakup.
memories.memory_text: I brought Hazel down to my basement to support Isaac during his emotional crisis, and I remember looking at her with my cigarette hanging from my mouth, knowing that pain demands to be felt.

grounded_facts: Gus pretends to read an email response from Peter Van Houten to Hazel, claiming the author has refused to write a sequel.
A shared imaginative act where Gus pretends to read an official email from Peter Van Houten in response to Hazel's earlier expressed desire for closure about the novel.
memories.memory_text: I pretended to read an email from Peter Van Houten to Hazel, telling her he refused to write a sequel, as part of our shared imaginative act after she mentioned wanting closure from him.

grounded_facts: Gus fabricates a letter from Van Houten to emotionally engage Hazel, surprising her with a simulated response to her deepest literary longing.
memories.memory_text: I made up the letter from Van Houten to surprise Hazel and emotionally engage her, knowing it touched her deepest literary longing, and later I asked her if she thought I could invent such a letter with my meager intellect.

grounded_facts: Hazel expresses shock, hope, and excitement in response to the fabricated letter, validating Gus's emotional intent.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel sit up in shock, stunned and jumping up with excitement, whispering 'Holy hell,' and I knew her hope had been sparked by the letter I created.

grounded_facts: Hazel reads her draft email aloud to Augustus to get his opinion on tone and content.
Hazel composes and reads aloud an email to Peter Van Houten, asking for answers about the aftermath of his novel and expressing deep admiration.
memories.memory_text: I listened as Hazel read her email aloud to me, telling me how she was writing to Van Houten to ask about his novel and expressing how much she admired him, even saying she’d read his grocery lists.

grounded_facts: Hazel spends the night composing a letter to Van Houten while on the phone with Augustus, who listens and provides feedback.
memories.memory_text: I stayed on the phone with Hazel while she spent the night composing that email, giving her my thoughts on it when she asked.

grounded_facts: Augustus evaluates Hazel's email as well-written and suitable for Van Houten's style, despite minor pretentiousness.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel the email was well-written and thought Van Houten would like it, even if it was a bit pretentious, since he uses words like 'tendentious' and 'bacchanalia'.

grounded_facts: After finishing the email, Hazel and Augustus prolong their phone call, exchanging multiple 'ok's, delaying the end of the interaction.
Hazel and Augustus repeatedly say 'ok' instead of hanging up, creating a tender, intimate ritual.
memories.memory_text: I said 'ok' to Hazel a few times after we finished the email, and she said it back, and we both laughed—we were just stalling because neither of us wanted to hang up. I even suggested that 'ok' could be our 'always,' and she smiled.

grounded_facts: Isaac expresses his belief in true love despite physical suffering.
memories.memory_text: I heard Isaac say that even though people suffer, everyone should have true love.

grounded_facts: Isaac uses his pain pump to administer morphine, leading to drowsiness and sleep.
memories.memory_text: I saw Isaac press the button on his pain pump and then get drowsy as the morphine took effect.

grounded_facts: Isaac begins to share information about Gus's visit but falls asleep before completing the thought.
memories.memory_text: I asked Isaac about my visit, but he fell asleep before he could tell me what he wanted to say.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus walk together on a suburban sidewalk, engaging in personal conversation.
memories.memory_text: I walked beside Hazel on the sidewalk, just talking as we strolled through the neighborhood.

grounded_facts: Hazel discloses that she used her wish to visit Disney World and Epcot Center when she was 13.
memories.memory_text: Hazel told me she used her wish to go to Disney World and Epcot Center when she was 13, and I remember her saying it like it was no big deal.

grounded_facts: Gus mocks Hazel for using her wish on Disney World, calling it cliché and sad.
memories.memory_text: I teased Hazel about using her wish on Disney, telling her it was the saddest thing I'd ever heard because it was so cliché.

grounded_facts: Gus unintentionally reveals he has a crush on Hazel, causing emotional shift in their interaction.
memories.memory_text: I mentioned having a crush on Hazel while teasing her about her Disney wish, not meaning to say it so directly.

grounded_facts: Hazel is surprised and flustered upon hearing Gus has a crush on her, blushing and trying to hide her excitement.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Hazel got flustered and looked away blushing after I said the word 'crush,' like she was trying to hide how surprised she felt.

grounded_facts: Gus is already waiting on the front stoop when Frannie's car pulls up, indicating his arrival prior to the family's return from the hospital.
memories.memory_text: I was already waiting on the front stoop when Frannie's car pulled up, so I could be there as soon as Hazel got home.

grounded_facts: Gus brings a bouquet of bright orange tulips and is present with them when Hazel arrives, implying the gift is intended for her.
memories.memory_text: I brought a bouquet of bright orange tulips and wore my Pacers jersey when I came over, wanting to surprise Hazel when she returned from the hospital.

grounded_facts: An informal and unanticipated gathering at Hazel's house upon her return from the hospital, initiated by Gus's presence.
memories.memory_text: I saw Michael help Hazel out of the car and I stood up to greet them, starting an unexpected gathering at her house.

grounded_facts: Michael notices and comments on Gus's Indiana Pacers jersey, identifying it as belonging to Rik Smits.
memories.memory_text: I was wearing my Indiana Pacers jersey when Michael noticed it and asked if it belonged to Rik Smits, and I confirmed that it was indeed his jersey.

grounded_facts: Gus acknowledges Hazel upon her arrival with a simple 'Hi Hazel,' following her surprised reaction.
memories.memory_text: I said 'Hi Hazel' when she arrived and noticed me.

grounded_facts: Gus asks Hazel if she would like to go on a picnic, marking a direct romantic or social overture.
memories.memory_text: I asked Hazel if she would like to go on a picnic with me.

grounded_facts: Gus discloses that he has been sober for fourteen months.
memories.memory_text: I told Michael that I've been sober for fourteen months.

grounded_facts: Michael informs Gus that Hazel is still very sick and will be for the rest of her life, particularly noting her lung condition.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Michael that Hazel is still very sick and will be for the rest of her life, especially because of her lungs.

grounded_facts: Hazel appears and asks Gus if he is ready, cutting off Michael's sentence about her health.
Hazel asks Gus if he is ready, signaling the transition from waiting to departure.
memories.memory_text: I was standing there when Michael started telling me Hazel was still pretty sick and would be for the rest of her life, but then she appeared and asked me if I was ready, cutting him off, and I knew it was time for us to leave.

grounded_facts: Gus uses a stick to draw circles in the dirt to humorously illustrate the rarity of 17-year-old guys with one leg who are still virgins.
memories.memory_text: I picked up a stick and drew a big circle in the dirt to joke about how rare it is for a 17-year-old guy with one leg to still be a virgin, showing Hazel with the drawing how small that group is.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus share a picnic in the gardens behind the Indianapolis Museum of Art, discussing life, literature, and love.
memories.memory_text: I remember walking with Hazel, then spreading a blanket near those giant white bones where kids were playing. I brought sandwiches and orange juice for our picnic, and we sat together eating and watching them. I remember saying, 'How cool is that? A skeleton being used as a playground,' just to share the moment with her.

grounded_facts: Gus explains that it wouldn't make sense to meet Peter Van Houten without Hazel, acknowledging her central role in his literary journey.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel that it wouldn't make much sense to meet Peter Van Houten without her, since she's the one who introduced me to his book.

grounded_facts: After questioning Gus's motives, Hazel initiates a kiss, confirming mutual romantic feelings.
memories.memory_text: After she questioned me, I saw her hug me tightly and then kiss me, which made it clear that we both felt something real.

grounded_facts: Hazel pauses the romantic moment to ask if Gus is only taking her to Amsterdam to get kissed.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel suddenly pausing and asking me if I was only taking her to Amsterdam so she'd kiss me, then pressing me to explain why I was really doing this.

grounded_facts: Gus states that meeting Hazel was his true wish, transforming the emotional meaning of the trip.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel that meeting her was my true wish, because I finally realized it was never about Amsterdam or Van Houten—it was about her.

grounded_facts: Gus reveals that he saved his wish and intends to use it to go to Amsterdam with Hazel to meet Peter Van Houten.
memories.memory_text: I revealed to Hazel that I still have my Wish, got it in exchange for my leg, and that I plan to use it to take her to Amsterdam—we're leaving on May third, because I finally found my real wish.

grounded_facts: Gus, unable to visit someone in the ICU due to family-only access, requests Michael to inform her that he was there waiting.
Gus asks Michael to inform the patient that he was there, showing emotional investment and respect for hospital rules.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't go into the ICU because only family was allowed, so I asked Michael to tell her I was there waiting—I needed her to know I hadn't left.

grounded_facts: A visit to the ICU waiting area by Gus and Michael, concerning the condition of a hospitalized individual.
memories.memory_text: I remember pacing in the waiting area, seeing Michael down the hall, and chasing after him—I just had to make sure she knew I was there, even if I couldn't see her.

grounded_facts: Michael expresses care for Gus's well-being by suggesting he go home and rest.
Michael, showing concern for Gus, advises him to go home and get some rest.
memories.memory_text: Michael called my name and then told me I should go home and get some rest, showing he really cares about how I'm doing.

grounded_facts: Hazel receives a text message from Gus asking 'ok?' but does not respond.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Hazel received my text asking 'ok?' but she didn't respond, which made me wonder if she was really okay.

grounded_facts: Gus sends a text message asking Hazel if she is ok, showing concern.
memories.memory_text: I sent Hazel a text asking if she was okay because I wanted to make sure she was alright after sensing she might be pulling away.

grounded_facts: Michael tells Hazel that Gus is on the phone, relaying an incoming communication.
memories.memory_text: I remember Michael coming into the room, whispering that Gus was on the phone again.

grounded_facts: Hazel sends a second text clarifying that she sees herself as a source of future pain for Augustus, reinforcing her decision to end the relationship.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed her send a second text after the silence, reinforcing that she sees herself as a source of future pain for me, which made it clear she was ending things to protect me.

grounded_facts: Hazel makes the emotional decision to end her relationship with Augustus to protect him from future pain caused by her illness.
memories.memory_text: I think she ended things because she believes I'll suffer when she dies, and she wanted to protect me from that pain, though I'm not sure it was the right call.

grounded_facts: Hazel uses the metaphor 'I'm a grenade' to express how she believes her death will emotionally destroy those close to her.
Hazel initiates emotional separation by texting Augustus that she can no longer be with him, citing her terminal illness.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel texting me that she can't be with me anymore, and she said, 'I'm a grenade,' like her death would blow me apart.

grounded_facts: Hazel tells Augustus that seeing him makes her anticipate the pain she will cause him when she dies.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel telling me she can't see me anymore because she believes I'll suffer when she dies — she said, 'When I look at you, all I can see is what I'm going to put you through,' and called herself a grenade.

grounded_facts: After the emotional exchange, Augustus responds to Hazel's 'Ok' with a joking remark about flirting, masking his hurt.
After receiving Hazel's serious messages, Augustus replies with humor to mask his pain, calling her 'flirting' in response to her 'Ok.'
memories.memory_text: After Hazel said 'Ok,' I could feel the weight of what she meant, so I joked, 'oh my god, stop flirting with me!' to hide how much it hurt.

grounded_facts: After crying and reflecting on her emotions, Hazel makes the decision to reach out to Gus by phone.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Hazel called me after she had been crying and reflecting on everything that was weighing on her.

grounded_facts: Gus uses humor to lighten Hazel's mood by demanding to see the 'swing set of tears,' which makes her smile.
memories.memory_text: I used humor to lighten the mood by telling Hazel I demanded to see the 'swing set of tears,' and I saw her smile, which made me glad.

grounded_facts: Gus responds to Hazel's call and comes to her backyard, transforming the emotional atmosphere.
memories.memory_text: I responded to Hazel's call and came to her backyard, and I could tell that my being there made things better between us.

grounded_facts: Gus tells Hazel that her attempts to distance herself will not reduce his feelings for her.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel that trying to keep her distance won't lessen my feelings for her, and that all her efforts to save me from herself will fail.

grounded_facts: Gus names the unspoken fear Hazel carries — that she will emotionally destroy those close to her when she dies — using the metaphor of a grenade.
memories.memory_text: I named Hazel's fear by saying 'Grenades,' then explained that I understand one day she might emotionally explode and everyone close to her will be caught in the wake.

grounded_facts: Hazel confirms Gus's metaphor that she is a 'grenade' who will emotionally destroy those close to her when she dies.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel nod and then say 'Exactly,' confirming that she sees herself as a grenade who will emotionally destroy those around her when she dies.

grounded_facts: A private, emotionally charged moment in Hazel's backyard where she breaks down, calls Gus, and they confront the risks of their growing closeness.
memories.memory_text: I remember being on the phone with Hazel in her backyard, hearing her pour out her sadness about the swing set her dad made, and I told her I demanded to see that swing set of tears—then we both just stood there quietly, looking at it, before I said we had to do something about that frigging swing set.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus collaboratively write a humorous Craigslist post about a swing set
memories.memory_text: I stood next to Hazel while she was writing a Craigslist post, and we worked together on it, making jokes about a swing set.

grounded_facts: Gus tells Hazel he likes her because she is uniquely herself, which marks a shift in emotional openness.
Gus compliments Hazel by explaining that her authentic self is what makes her special, strengthening emotional intimacy
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel that's why I like her—because she's so busy being herself that she doesn't even realize how utterly unprecedented she is, and I meant it.

grounded_facts: The swing set is delivered and loaded into the townie's pick-up truck, marking the completion of its installation at Hazel's house.
memories.memory_text: I watched with Hazel as the townie finished loading the swing set into his pick-up truck, and I gave it a little salute as he drove off—it felt like a moment worth marking.

grounded_facts: Gus sneaks a quick kiss on Hazel's cheek, initiating a moment of intimacy that she responds to with mild disapproval.
memories.memory_text: I leaned in and gave Hazel a quick kiss on the cheek, just because I could feel the moment was right.

grounded_facts: In response to Gus's cheek kiss, Hazel playfully elbows him away, indicating mild protest with affectionate undertones.
memories.memory_text: She playfully elbowed me away after I kissed her, so I know she wasn’t really mad—just keeping me in check.

grounded_facts: The coordinated effort to confirm and prepare for Hazel and family's trip to Amsterdam with Augustus Waters.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel texting me 'STILL FREE MAY 3? :-)' and realizing we were still on for Amsterdam — it made me hopeful that the trip was still happening, though I wasn't completely sure until more plans came through.

grounded_facts: Hazel texts Augustus to confirm his availability on May 3, signaling her renewed hope and excitement about the trip.
Hazel sends a text to Gus asking if he is free on May 3, using a cheerful tone with a smiley face.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel texting me, asking if I was free on May 3 with a smiley face, and I felt her hope—so I replied right away with excitement, knowing everything was still on track for our trip.

grounded_facts: Frannie and Hazel arrive at Gus's house, preparing to pick him up for their trip to Amsterdam.
memories.memory_text: I was waiting for Frannie and Hazel to pick me up at my house, ready to go on our trip to Amsterdam.

grounded_facts: Frannie and Hazel hear a heated argument between Gus and his mother before being seen.
memories.memory_text: I was inside my house when Frannie and Hazel arrived, and I didn't realize they were at the door until after my mom and I had our argument. I later found out they heard me yelling about my life belonging to me before quietly leaving.

grounded_facts: Frannie physically turns Hazel away from the house and explains they shouldn't listen in.
memories.memory_text: Frannie told me we shouldn't eavesdrop on what was happening inside, and then she turned me around and walked me back to the car with her.

grounded_facts: Frannie intervenes and leads Hazel back to the car to avoid eavesdropping on Gus's private argument.
memories.memory_text: I saw Frannie pull Hazel and me back to the car, steering us away from the house so we wouldn't overhear something private.

grounded_facts: Gus exits his house with luggage, joining Frannie and Hazel for the trip.
memories.memory_text: I walked out of my house with my travel bag and a cigarette in my mouth, ready to join Frannie and Hazel for the trip.

grounded_facts: Gus politely greets Frannie and then exchanges a hesitant 'ok' with Hazel.
memories.memory_text: I greeted Frannie politely, saying it was always a pleasure to see her, then turned to Hazel and said, 'Hello, Hazel Grace,' and after her hesitant 'ok...?' I replied, 'Ok.'

grounded_facts: A planned journey to Amsterdam involving Frannie, Hazel, and Gus.
memories.memory_text: I was told we were going to Amsterdam, and Frannie announced it excitedly to me and Hazel.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus go through airport security, requiring Hazel to temporarily remove her oxygen equipment.
memories.memory_text: I went through airport security with Hazel, and she had to take off her oxygen equipment for the checkpoint.

grounded_facts: Hazel unhooks the plastic nubbins from her nose before going through the security checkpoint, temporarily going without oxygen.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel unhook the plastic nubbins from her nose before walking through the metal detector, going without oxygen for a while.

grounded_facts: After walking through the metal detector without oxygen, Hazel shows signs of physical distress and must steady herself.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Hazel struggling after she walked through the metal detector without oxygen, and she had to steady herself on the other side.

grounded_facts: Hazel reinserts the oxygen cannula as soon as her tank is available, restoring her oxygen intake.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel immediately reinsert her oxygen cannula as soon as her tank was returned to her.

grounded_facts: Hazel catches her mom looking nervously and responds with a determined, though labored, declaration of their destination.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Hazel catch her mom looking at her nervously, and though it was hard for her, she responded by declaring 'Amsterdam!'—I think she was trying to reassure her mom, but I can't be sure how she really felt.

grounded_facts: Despite being light-headed, Hazel declares 'Amsterdam!' with some difficulty, signaling determination and emotional focus.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel, even though she was light-headed, push through and say 'Amsterdam!' with effort, showing how determined she was.

grounded_facts: A young couple gives up their seats at the airport gate for Hazel and Gus, who accept them.
memories.memory_text: I remember a young couple getting up so Hazel and I could have their seats at the airport gate, and we accepted them.

grounded_facts: Hazel removes her oxygen cannula and lets a curious little girl try it, creating a brief but meaningful interaction.
Hazel calmly explains the function of her oxygen cannula to a curious child and allows her to try it.
memories.memory_text: I watched Hazel calmly explain her oxygen cannula to a curious little girl, and then I saw her take it off and let the child try it, which created a brief but meaningful moment between them before they smiled and waved goodbye.

grounded_facts: The airport announces the start of pre-boarding for Flight 144 to Amsterdam, specifically calling passengers needing extra assistance.
memories.memory_text: I heard the airport announcement calling for pre-boarding on Flight 144 to Amsterdam, specifically for passengers who needed extra assistance.

grounded_facts: The organized process of pre-boarding begins for Flight 144 to Amsterdam, targeting passengers requiring extra assistance.
memories.memory_text: I heard the announcement for pre-boarding Flight 144 to Amsterdam for passengers who need extra assistance, and Hazel said, 'I think that's us,' which made me realize it was time for us to board.

grounded_facts: Gus places a cigarette in his mouth to symbolize control over death, explaining it is not literal smoking.
memories.memory_text: I put a cigarette in my mouth to remind myself that I can face death without letting it win, and when the flight attendant noticed, I nodded and put it away after explaining I don't actually smoke.

grounded_facts: Moved by Gus's childlike wonder at flying, Hazel kisses him on the cheek.
memories.memory_text: I felt Hazel lean over and kiss me on the cheek while we were watching the movie, and it surprised me—she must have noticed how amazed I was, like a kid seeing the sky for the first time.

grounded_facts: Frannie reminds Hazel and Gus of her presence, disrupting their intimate moment.
memories.memory_text: I remember Frannie interrupting our moment by saying, 'Just so you know, I'm right here. Sitting next to you. Your mother,' which broke the quiet intimacy we had during the movie.

grounded_facts: When Hazel claims they are just friends, Gus openly states he is not, implying romantic interest.
memories.memory_text: When Hazel said we were just friends, I told her, 'She is. I'm not,' making it clear to her—and to Frannie—that I see us as something more.

grounded_facts: Gus, who has never been on a plane before, experiences takeoff and flight for the first time, showing initial nervousness that turns into wonder.
memories.memory_text: I'd never been on a plane before, and as we started taxiing, I felt my nerves spike—I even put a cigarette in my mouth to steady myself, though I couldn't light it. My hands gripped the armrest, heart racing, but once we were airborne and I saw the world below, I couldn't help but get caught up in the wonder of it all.

grounded_facts: A commercial airplane journey with Hazel, Gus, and Frannie aboard, involving takeoff, mid-flight movie watching, and landing.
memories.memory_text: I remember sitting by the window on the plane with Hazel in the middle and Frannie on the aisle; I grabbed her hand during takeoff because I was nervous, and later we watched a gory action movie together while Frannie slept.

grounded_facts: During the flight, Hazel observes Gus watching a movie and realizes she is falling in love with him.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Hazel watching me more than the movie, and I think she was realizing she might be falling for me—I couldn’t be sure, but there was something in the way she looked at me.

grounded_facts: The cab driver makes a sarcastic remark about Indiana being named after the Indians while stealing from them.
memories.memory_text: I heard the cab driver make a sarcastic comment about how Indiana is named after the Indians while they stole the land from them.

grounded_facts: The cab driver explains that Amsterdam expands in rings, growing older toward the center, which reframes the group's understanding of the city's geography.
memories.memory_text: I was in the cab with Hazel and Frannie when the driver explained that Amsterdam expands in rings, getting older toward the center, like the rings of a tree.

grounded_facts: Hazel questions whether the current location is truly Amsterdam, prompting the driver's explanation of the city's structure.
memories.memory_text: I heard Hazel ask the driver if this was really Amsterdam, and then I learned from the driver that the city is like tree rings, getting older as you move toward the center.

grounded_facts: The group visually enters the historic center of Amsterdam, marked by canals, row houses, houseboats, and bicycles, creating a transformative impression.
memories.memory_text: I saw the colorful row houses, canals, houseboats, and bicycles as we entered central Amsterdam, and it struck me how different and beautiful it was.

grounded_facts: The group enters the outskirts of Amsterdam, characterized by flat, dusty landscape and industrial structures, setting up a contrast with the expected city center.
memories.memory_text: I saw the outskirts of Amsterdam as we arrived, with a flat, dusty landscape and concrete buildings that made me realize we hadn't yet reached the historic center.

grounded_facts: A taxi ride carrying Hazel, Gus, and Frannie from the highway into central Amsterdam, during which they observe the changing landscape and receive commentary from the driver.
memories.memory_text: I was in the back of a yellow cab with Hazel and Frannie, riding into Amsterdam and watching the landscape change from flat and dusty to colorful row houses, houseboats, and people biking on cobblestone streets.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Frannie arrive at the hotel room, where Gus helps them bring their belongings inside.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Hazel and Frannie arrive at the hotel room, where Gus helps them bring their belongings inside.

grounded_facts: Gus tells Hazel he will be nearby, offering comfort and support.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Gus tells Hazel he will be nearby, offering comfort and support.

grounded_facts: Hazel, exhausted, sits on the bed and begins to drift off to sleep after arriving in the hotel room.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Hazel, exhausted, sits on the bed and begins to drift off to sleep after arriving in the hotel room.

grounded_facts: Frannie promises to do 'crazy Mom stuff' that night to give Hazel freedom for her date with Gus.
memories.memory_text: I remember Frannie telling me she’d do 'crazy Mom stuff' that night so I’d have freedom for the date with me and Gus.

grounded_facts: A planned romantic dinner at Oranjee in Amsterdam, arranged by Mr. Van Houten for Hazel and Gus.
memories.memory_text: I was told we had reservations at a fancy and romantic place called Oranjee in Amsterdam, set up by Mr. Van Houten.

grounded_facts: Frannie informs Hazel that she has a dinner reservation at Oranjee arranged by Mr. Van Houten.
memories.memory_text: I recall Frannie telling me that I had a dinner reservation at a place called Oranjee, arranged by Mr. Van Houten.

grounded_facts: Hazel sarcastically questions whether her mother truly approves of her spending unsupervised time with Gus in a foreign city.
memories.memory_text: I heard Hazel sarcastically ask her mom if it was really okay for a 16-year-old girl to be running free with an older boy like me in a foreign city known for vice and debauchery.

grounded_facts: Frannie avoids addressing Hazel's concern directly and instead expresses excitement about getting Hazel dressed.
memories.memory_text: I saw Frannie avoid answering Hazel's question and instead get excited about getting Hazel dressed.

grounded_facts: Gus arrives at the hotel room wearing a perfectly tailored black suit, signaling readiness for a formal outing.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at the hotel room in my perfectly tailored black suit, ready for our evening out.

grounded_facts: Gus expresses admiration for Hazel's look, affirming her self-presentation and easing her concern about being under-dressed.
Gus tells Hazel she looks gorgeous in response to her insecurity about her outfit.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel she looked gorgeous when she asked if she was under-dressed, and I meant it—she really did look amazing.

grounded_facts: A planned social event or date that Hazel and Gus are preparing to attend, marked by formal attire and physical coordination.
memories.memory_text: I think we were both getting ready for a formal event—I was dressed up and we ended up leaving together, so it must have been something special.

grounded_facts: Hazel comes out of the bathroom wearing a knee-length pale blue sundress, presenting herself for evaluation before the outing.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel come out of the bathroom in a knee-length pale blue sundress, and I offered her my arm before we left together.

grounded_facts: Hazel takes Gus's offered arm, accepting his gesture of escort.
Hazel takes Gus's offered arm, signaling mutual readiness and physical coordination for departure.
memories.memory_text: I offered Hazel my arm, and she took it—our connection clicked into place, signaling we were both ready to leave together.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus ride together on a tram through Amsterdam at night, observing the cityscape and beginning their evening.
memories.memory_text: I rode the tram with Hazel through Amsterdam at night, taking in the cityscape as we began our evening together.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus are offered seats by an old couple on the tram, which they accept after a failed attempt by Hazel to protest.
The old couple offers their seats to Hazel and Gus, ignoring Hazel's protest, creating a small moment of kindness and social ritual.
memories.memory_text: An old couple offered us their seats on the tram, and even though Hazel tried to protest, they ignored her and we ended up sitting down, accepting their quiet act of kindness.

grounded_facts: Gus expresses strong admiration for Hazel's appearance, specifically her dress.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel I was stunned by how she looked, that her dress was something special—like whoa—because I wanted her to know I noticed.

grounded_facts: A romantic dinner for Hazel and Gus at Oranjee Restaurant by the canal in Amsterdam, featuring champagne, fine dining, and deep conversation.
memories.memory_text: I remember how we sat by the water at Oranjee, and I pulled out Hazel's chair before the champagne was poured; we toasted under a sky full of stars and shared a quiet thank you across the table as we enjoyed our meal together.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus share personal stories about their 'death suits,' revealing vulnerabilities tied to their illnesses.
memories.memory_text: I shared with Hazel how losing my leg felt like wearing a death suit, and she told me she had one too, bought for her 15th birthday—so we both laid that fear bare between courses.

grounded_facts: Gus playfully confirms whether their evening qualifies as a date.
memories.memory_text: I asked Hazel if we were on a date, just like that, because I wanted to know where we stood in that moment.

grounded_facts: Gus confesses his deep love to Hazel, expressing both existential awareness and emotional commitment.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel I'm in love with her, even though I know love is just a shout into the void and that everything ends in oblivion—I said it all, and I meant it.

grounded_facts: The waiter reveals that Mr. Van Houten has already paid for the entire meal.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting there with Hazel when the waiter came over and told me that Mr. Van Houten had already paid for our meal.

grounded_facts: Gus arrives at the hotel room and announces that it's time to seek answers, signaling a transition in the narrative.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at the hotel room, knocked, and when I poked my head in, I said, 'Who's ready for some answers!'—it was time to stop waiting and start moving.

grounded_facts: Gus makes a sarcastic comment about Hazel's excitement, lightening the mood momentarily.
memories.memory_text: I made a sarcastic comment about Hazel's excitement, saying, 'As opposed to other days...?' to lighten the mood.

grounded_facts: Gus and Hazel arrive at Van Houten's house and wait to be let in.
memories.memory_text: I stood with Hazel outside Van Houten's white house, waiting after she knocked on the door, and we looked at each other in silence, wondering if anyone would answer.

grounded_facts: Peter Van Houten slams the door in Gus and Hazel's faces after recognizing them.
memories.memory_text: I saw the man in pajamas slam the door in our faces after he recognized us, and I couldn't believe he'd just shut us out like that.

grounded_facts: Gus and Hazel confirm that the man in pajamas is Peter Van Houten through overheard dialogue.
memories.memory_text: I overheard the conversation through the door and realized the man in pajamas was Peter Van Houten—I couldn't believe it was really him.

grounded_facts: Lidewij challenges Van Houten's behavior and insists he be civil.
memories.memory_text: I saw Lidewij stand up to Van Houten and tell him to be nice, and then she opened the door for us.

grounded_facts: Van Houten asks which one is Augustus Waters, acknowledging Gus formally.
memories.memory_text: I remember Van Houten looking at us and asking, 'Which of you is Augustus Waters?' as if he needed to pick me out.

grounded_facts: A planned meeting between Gus, Hazel, and author Peter Van Houten, which begins with tension and hostility.
memories.memory_text: I was part of a meeting with Hazel and Peter Van Houten that started with tension and hostility—I heard his voice through the door, couldn't believe he was really there, and then saw him being pushed toward us by his assistant before he silently walked away, leaving the door open.

grounded_facts: Van Houten refuses to meet Gus and Hazel, expressing disdain for Americans.
memories.memory_text: I heard Van Houten tell Lidewij he left America to avoid Americans and wanted us gone, and then he just walked away without saying a word to us.

grounded_facts: After initial rejection, Gus and Hazel are allowed entry into Van Houten's house.
memories.memory_text: After being shut out at first, I took the first step inside with Hazel right behind me when we were finally allowed in.

grounded_facts: A planned visit by Hazel and Gus to meet author Peter Van Houten at his home for a discussion about his novel.
memories.memory_text: I remember arriving with Hazel at Van Houten's house, where we were led into a sterile living room and took our seats, ready to talk about his book.

grounded_facts: Van Houten accuses Hazel of seeking pity due to her illness, undermining her emotional investment in the characters.
memories.memory_text: I saw Van Houten accuse Hazel of seeking pity because of her illness, telling her she’s fated to stay a child who believes in life after a novel, and it made me feel angry and protective.

grounded_facts: Shocked and hurt by Van Houten's cruelty, Lidewij declares she is resigning as his assistant.
memories.memory_text: I heard Lidewij shout 'I RESIGN!' after Van Houten's cruel remarks, and I could tell she was deeply hurt.

grounded_facts: Hazel directly challenges Van Houten to fulfill his implied promise to reveal what happens after the end of his book.
memories.memory_text: I watched Hazel challenge Van Houten directly, demanding he tell us what happens to his characters, and I stood with her, hoping he’d finally give us an answer.

grounded_facts: Van Houten asserts that fictional characters have no life beyond the text, rejecting Hazel's belief in their continued existence.
Van Houten dismisses Hazel and Gus's inquiry about the fates of the characters after the end of his novel, asserting they are fictions that cease to exist.
memories.memory_text: I heard Van Houten say the characters cease to exist after the novel ends, and when Hazel tried to push back, he refused to say more, shutting us down completely.

grounded_facts: After Van Houten continues to refuse answering, Hazel physically disrupts his attempt to drink by slapping the glass from his hand.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel slap the glass right out of Van Houten's hand, surprising everyone in the room.

grounded_facts: A planned encounter between Hazel, Gus, and author Peter Van Houten, intended to seek answers about his novel, which ends in emotional disappointment.
memories.memory_text: I was there with Hazel when we finally met Van Houten, hoping he’d give us answers about his book, but it all just fell apart and left us both shaken.

grounded_facts: Hazel responds to Van Houten's condescending question with a profane dismissal.
Hazel responds to Van Houten's dismissive question with anger, telling him to 'go fuck yourself,' marking a definitive emotional break.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel snap at Van Houten when he asked why she even cared about his stupid questions, and she told him to go fuck himself—I felt that moment like a door slamming shut.

grounded_facts: To comfort Hazel, Gus offers to write her a sequel to the novel, better than Van Houten could, reigniting hope and emotional connection.
Gus hugs Hazel and promises to write her a sequel to comfort her after the traumatic meeting.
memories.memory_text: I hugged Hazel and told her it was going to be okay, then promised I’d write her a sequel—something better than anything that drunk could come up with, full of blood and guts and real sacrifice, just for her.

grounded_facts: Hazel expresses guilt over spending her Wish on Van Houten, but Gus reframes it as an experience shared between them.
Gus reassures Hazel that their trip was not wasted on Van Houten but was instead an experience they shared.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel saying she spent my Wish on that asshole, and I told her she didn't spend it on him—she spent it on us.

grounded_facts: Lidewij emerges to apologize, acknowledging Van Houten's cruelty and expressing regret that the meeting did not go as hoped.
Lidewij expresses regret for Van Houten's behavior and explains her failed hope that the meeting would help him.
memories.memory_text: I heard Lidewij apologize, saying she was sorry for Van Houten's cruelty and that she had hoped meeting us would help him, but it didn't.

grounded_facts: Gus declares he will not participate in any activity connected to Van Houten, asserting emotional boundaries.
Gus refuses to engage in any activity associated with Van Houten, even indirectly.
memories.memory_text: I made it clear that I wouldn't go anywhere with that monster Van Houten, and I refused to take part in anything connected to him, to protect Hazel and myself.

grounded_facts: Lidewij reports that there is no elevator at the Anne Frank House, only steep stairs, which presents a physical access challenge.
Lidewij delivers the disappointing news that there is no elevator and only steep stairs at the Anne Frank House.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Lidewij that there's no elevator at the Anne Frank House, only steep stairs, which made me worry about how Hazel would manage.

grounded_facts: Hazel responds to Gus's concern by firmly asserting her ability and intention to climb the stairs.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel respond firmly when I expressed concern, saying 'I can do it!' and showing she was determined to climb the stairs.

grounded_facts: Hazel refuses to accept limitation due to disability, asserting her determination to enter the Anne Frank House despite the lack of elevator and presence of steep stairs.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Hazel refuse to let her disability stop her, standing her ground and asserting her determination to climb the steep stairs and enter the house.

grounded_facts: A planned group visit to the Anne Frank House, involving ticket purchase and entry despite accessibility challenges.
memories.memory_text: I was part of the group that went to visit the Anne Frank House, and I remember we got the tickets and were going inside despite the challenges.

grounded_facts: Lidewij provides factual and emotional context about the Frank family's fate during the tour.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Lidewij that the bookcase hid the Frank family and four others, and she shared it with emotional weight that made me feel the gravity of what happened.

grounded_facts: Hazel overcomes physical difficulty to climb the narrow, steep stairs to the final hiding room, symbolizing her determination and resilience.
memories.memory_text: I watched Hazel climb the narrow, steep stairs with great difficulty, hearing her labored breathing and seeing her stumble near the top before pulling herself through and collapsing against the wall to catch her breath.

grounded_facts: Gus comforts Hazel as she struggles to breathe, affirming her strength.
memories.memory_text: I came to Hazel's side when she was struggling, wiped her brow, crouched beside her, and told her, 'You're a champion,' because I could see how hard she was fighting to keep going.

grounded_facts: A guided visit to the historical hiding place of Anne Frank and her family, attended by Hazel, Gus, Lidewij, and other travelers.
memories.memory_text: I stood with Hazel and Lidewij among a group of travelers at the start of the tour, and we both slowly climbed the stairs together as part of the visit to Anne Frank's hiding place.

grounded_facts: After watching the video about Anne Frank's final days, Hazel kisses Gus in a deeply emotional and intense moment, affirming their bond.
memories.memory_text: I remember that After watching the video about Anne Frank's final days, Hazel kisses Gus in a deeply emotional and intense moment, affirming their bond.

grounded_facts: After the couple kisses, the surrounding tourists applaud and one shouts 'bravo,' showing emotional approval.
memories.memory_text: I remember that After the couple kisses, the surrounding tourists applaud and one shouts 'bravo,' showing emotional approval.

grounded_facts: Gus informs Hazel that his leg is amputated above the knee, expressing nervousness about her reaction.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel that my leg is amputated above the knee, explaining how it tapers and then it's just skin, because I wanted her to be prepared before we went any further.

grounded_facts: Hazel responds to Gus's nervous revelation about his leg by telling him to stop being self-conscious, showing acceptance.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel about my leg, feeling nervous, and she looked at me and said, 'Oh get over yourself,' which made me realize she wasn't repulsed or even fazed by it.

grounded_facts: Gus tries to take off Hazel's shirt, but becomes entangled with her oxygen tube, leading to shared laughter.
memories.memory_text: I tried to take Hazel's shirt off, but it got tangled in her oxygen tube and I couldn't figure it out—we ended up just laughing together.

grounded_facts: A private, emotionally and physically intimate encounter between Gus and Hazel in his hotel room following a date.
memories.memory_text: I remember falling onto my bed with Hazel, kissing her, and then laughing together when my attempt to take her shirt off got ruined by her oxygen tube getting tangled.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus verbally confess their love for each other during an intimate moment.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel I loved her too, right after she said she loved me, and in that moment I knew we both meant it.

grounded_facts: Gus discovers a note left by Hazel upon waking up, which contains a personal message and a diagram about relationships.
Gus reads and understands the Venn diagram in Hazel's note, recognizing the humorous exclusion of certain qualities in romantic partners.
memories.memory_text: I woke up and found a note from Hazel on the bed, and when I read it, I saw she'd drawn a funny Venn diagram about relationships that made me smile because I got the joke about 17-year-old dudes with one leg not quite fitting in with virgins.

grounded_facts: Hazel, Gus, and Frannie meet at an outdoor cafe during the day, drinking coffee and discussing recent events.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting with Hazel and Frannie at an outdoor cafe, drinking coffee in the sun and talking about what had happened recently.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus re-enact a past argument where Hazel told Gus to get up and he refused, calling standing 'for fools'.
memories.memory_text: I re-enacted a past argument with Hazel where she told me to get up and I refused, saying 'Standing is for fools!'—we both giggled at how dramatic it was.

grounded_facts: Frannie excuses herself from the cafe table to give Hazel and Gus private time to talk.
memories.memory_text: I saw Frannie excuse herself from the table, saying she'd stretch her legs to give Hazel and me some private time to talk.

grounded_facts: Hazel remarks that Frannie's sudden departure was weird.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel saying to me, 'That was weird,' about Frannie's sudden departure.

grounded_facts: Gus does not respond to Hazel's comment about Frannie's departure, instead suggesting they move on.
memories.memory_text: I didn't respond to Hazel's comment about Frannie leaving—I just suggested we move on by asking, 'Shall we?'

grounded_facts: Gus discloses to Hazel that his cancer has returned and spread widely, as confirmed by a PET scan.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel that my PET scan lit up like a Christmas tree, that the cancer was in the lining of my chest, my liver, everywhere.

grounded_facts: A walk taken by Hazel and Gus through Amsterdam after a period of silence, during which Gus reveals his cancer recurrence.
memories.memory_text: I remember walking through Amsterdam with Hazel after telling her, how she grabbed my arm and then fell into me, hugging me tightly while I struggled to hold it together.

grounded_facts: After Gus reveals his cancer has returned, Hazel hugs him tightly and apologizes, offering deep emotional comfort.
memories.memory_text: I felt Hazel hug me for dear life and heard her say through her tears, 'I'm so sorry, Augustus,' and I let her hold me, even though I wanted to be the strong one.

grounded_facts: Gus reflects on the unfairness of life, stating that the world is not a wish-granting factory.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel that apparently the world is not a wish-granting factory, saying it like a joke but meaning it deep in my bones.

grounded_facts: Hazel tells Gus she is very fond of him, affirming emotional intimacy despite the grim news.
memories.memory_text: Hazel said she's very fond of me, and in that moment, I felt truly seen and close to her despite everything.

grounded_facts: Gus asks Hazel if she can treat him as if he isn't dying, revealing his desire to be seen beyond his illness.
memories.memory_text: I asked Hazel if she could forget about it and treat me like I'm not dying, because I wanted her to see me as more than just someone sick.

grounded_facts: Hazel tells Gus she doesn't think he's dying, calling his condition 'a touch of cancer' to minimize its weight and offer hope.
memories.memory_text: Hazel told me she doesn't think I'm dying, that I just have a touch of cancer, and I could hear her trying to make it feel smaller, lighter.

grounded_facts: Gus suggests kissing Hazel in the moment, seeking connection and normalcy amid emotional pain.
memories.memory_text: I asked Hazel if it would be absolutely ludicrous to make out right then, hoping she'd say yes because I needed to feel close to her, to feel normal even for a moment.

grounded_facts: In response to Gus's question, Hazel kisses him passionately without speaking.
memories.memory_text: She didn't say anything, but then she kissed me—hard—and I felt her answer more than I felt the kiss itself, like she was holding me together without words.

grounded_facts: The airplane departs from Amsterdam, marking the end of the trip.
Hazel rests on Gus's shoulder during the flight, showing intimacy and comfort.
memories.memory_text: I felt Hazel rest her head on my shoulder as we left Amsterdam behind, the city fading in the window while I stayed awake, present in the quiet moment we shared.

grounded_facts: Gus attempts to shake Michael's hand, but Michael instead embraces him in a hug, indicating acceptance and affection.
memories.memory_text: I reached out to shake Michael's hand, but instead he pulled me into a hug, which made me feel like I was really part of the family.

grounded_facts: A planned meeting at the Indianapolis Airport baggage claim where Michael reunites with his wife, Hazel, and Gus after their return.
Michael sees Hazel, her mother, and Gus arriving at the baggage claim and emotionally welcomes them, hugging each family member including Gus.
memories.memory_text: I saw Michael waiting for us at the baggage claim with a sign that said 'My Beautiful Family (and Gus),' and when we arrived, he hugged Hazel, kissed his wife, and then came over to me and the others.

grounded_facts: When Isaac accidentally touches Gus's thigh, Gus jokingly says 'Whoa, I'm taken,' deflecting physical contact with humor.
memories.memory_text: I joked 'Whoa, I'm taken' when Isaac accidentally touched my thigh, using humor to deflect the moment.

grounded_facts: Isaac jokingly asks Hazel if she has written Gus's eulogy yet, unintentionally revealing Gus's unspoken wish.
memories.memory_text: I heard Isaac ask Hazel if she'd written my eulogy yet, which made me realize he knew how I felt about it.

grounded_facts: A future event where Gus envisions having speakers, especially Hazel, deliver eulogies.
Gus asks Hazel to write a eulogy for his funeral, specifying that he wants her to be the primary speaker.
memories.memory_text: I imagined having speakers at my funeral and asked Hazel directly if she'd be kind enough to write my eulogy, especially wanting her to be the main one.

grounded_facts: Hazel lightly hits Isaac on the arm after he makes a teasing comment about her and Gus being adorable.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hazel playfully slap Isaac on the arm after he told us we were adorable.

grounded_facts: Isaac mentions a new girl in Support Group, indicating he is trying to move forward emotionally.
memories.memory_text: I saw Isaac mention a new girl in Support Group, trying to move on, and I realized he was shifting his focus away from Monica.

grounded_facts: Isaac discloses that Monica has not contacted him since their breakup, not even to check on his health.
memories.memory_text: I heard Isaac say that Monica hasn't reached out to him at all since their breakup, not even to ask how he's doing, and I felt angry about how she was treating him.

grounded_facts: Isaac begins throwing eggs at Monica's car under Gus's guidance, marking the start of a symbolic act of revenge.
Gus verbally directs Isaac, who is blind, to adjust his aim while throwing eggs.
memories.memory_text: I guided Isaac as he started throwing eggs at Monica's car, helping him adjust his aim by telling him to aim a little to the left.

grounded_facts: One of Isaac's eggs strikes the car door directly, setting off the alarm.
memories.memory_text: I saw one of Isaac's eggs hit the car door dead on, and the alarm immediately went off, making him pause for a second.

grounded_facts: Gus addresses Monica's mother with a theatrical declaration of moral justice.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Gus addresses Monica's mother with a theatrical declaration of moral justice.

grounded_facts: Monica's mother emerges, is addressed by Gus, and returns inside without confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Monica's mother emerges, is addressed by Gus, and returns inside without confrontation.

grounded_facts: Hazel expresses affection for Gus by kissing him on the cheek during the event.
Hazel kisses Gus on the cheek as a gesture of affection and admiration.
memories.memory_text: I felt Hazel gently kiss me on the cheek, a sweet gesture that let me know how much she admired and cared for me in that moment.

grounded_facts: A group act of symbolic revenge where Hazel, Gus, and Isaac throw eggs at Monica's car.
memories.memory_text: I was part of it when Hazel, Isaac, and I threw eggs at Monica's car, and I remember Hazel gently kissing me on the cheek during it.

grounded_facts: Hazel chooses to stay in the waiting room, sitting in the same chair Gus once occupied while waiting for her, symbolizing a role reversal and emotional continuity.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel sitting in the same chair I once waited in for her, and it felt like we'd switched places — she's waiting now, just like I did, though I'm not sure how much longer this connection will last.

grounded_facts: Hazel expresses anger and frustration toward Gus's preoccupation with being remembered, challenging his belief that a meaningful life requires widespread recognition.
Hazel angrily confronts Gus for prioritizing legacy over the love and life they share, asserting that her remembrance and affection should be enough.
memories.memory_text: Hazel stood up and confronted me, angry, telling me that my obsession with being remembered was pushing her away, and she asked if her love and remembrance weren't enough — if I couldn't be happy with just what we have together.

grounded_facts: After Hazel's emotional outburst, Gus abandons his fixation on posthumous fame and accepts the significance of personal love and connection.
memories.memory_text: I used to think I needed a grand story for everyone to remember me, but after Hazel called me out, I realized how wrong I was — she told me she’d love and remember me, and that had to be enough.

grounded_facts: A second picnic between Hazel and Gus at the Indianapolis Museum of Art, featuring champagne in Winnie the Pooh cups, set on a hill overlooking the 'Funky Bones' art installation.
memories.memory_text: I was in my wheelchair at the picnic with Hazel on the hill overlooking the 'Funky Bones' art installation, and we shared champagne in Winnie the Pooh cups, toasting to us.

grounded_facts: Gus acknowledges Hazel is right, apologizes, and toasts to their life together, signaling emotional reconnection.
memories.memory_text: I told Hazel she was right, apologized, and raised my cup to toast our life together, because I meant it — this life with her is good.

grounded_facts: Gus calls Hazel late at night from a gas station, indicating something is wrong and asking for her help.
Gus, sounding weak, calls Hazel and asks her to come help him at the gas station because something is wrong.
A phone call initiated by Gus to Hazel at 2:35am, breaking normal communication patterns and signaling emergency.
memories.memory_text: I called Hazel at 2:35am from the gas station, knowing it was late and out of the ordinary, but I needed her help — I could barely speak, and I told her something was wrong and she had to come.

grounded_facts: Gus desperately begs Hazel not to call emergency services, expressing that he will never forgive her if she does.
memories.memory_text: I begged Hazel not to call 911, pleading with her because I meant it—I'd never forgive her if she did.

grounded_facts: Despite Gus's desperate pleas not to, Hazel decides to call emergency services, marking a turning point in his loss of control over his final moments.
memories.memory_text: I saw her pull out her phone and dial, even though I'd begged her not to—I realized I couldn't stop her, and that I was losing control over what happens to me.

grounded_facts: Gus sits alone in his car at a gas station, physically deteriorated and emotionally broken, after attempting a small act of independence by buying cigarettes.
memories.memory_text: I was alone in my car at the gas station, burning up with fever, my stomach bright red and leaking from the tube, too weak to even turn my head when I threw up—I just broke down, weeping because I couldn’t pretend I was okay anymore.

grounded_facts: Hazel locates Gus alone in his car at the Speedway gas station, discovering him in critical condition with a visibly infected G-tube site and high fever.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel opening my door and seeing me like that—covered in vomit and blood, hands pressed to my belly—she touched my forehead and knew how bad it was, and I couldn’t hide it from her anymore.

grounded_facts: Emergency medical technicians respond to a call and transport Gus to the hospital after Hazel dials 911.
memories.memory_text: I didn’t want her to call 911, but she did—I remember the EMTs loading me into the ambulance while I just lay there, helpless.

grounded_facts: Hazel rides with Gus in the ambulance as he drifts in and out of consciousness, during which he requests poetry and she composes a personal verse for him.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Hazel’s hand in the ambulance and asked her to read me something—she made up a poem, and I smiled, barely conscious, as she cradled my head in her arms.

grounded_facts: EMTs transport Gus to the hospital in an ambulance, with Hazel permitted to ride along, signifying the end of his autonomous outing.
memories.memory_text: I remember the EMTs loading me into the ambulance, and I was barely conscious, but I knew Hazel was with me, cradling my head in her arms as we rode to the hospital.

grounded_facts: Hazel reads and then improvises a poem for Gus in the ambulance to soothe him as he fades in and out of consciousness.
To comfort Gus during the ambulance ride, Hazel improvises a poetic variation on 'The Red Wheelbarrow,' personalizing it to his condition and their moment.
memories.memory_text: I heard Hazel read a poem to me in the ambulance, and then she made up her own version, something about an observer of the universe, and I felt her cradling my head as I smiled weakly.

grounded_facts: Gus comes back to his house after being discharged from the hospital, physically unwell but alive.
memories.memory_text: I came home from the hospital, and though I wasn't feeling well, I was alive.

grounded_facts: Hazel supports Gus physically as he enters the house after returning from the hospital.
memories.memory_text: I remember Hazel helping me inside the house when I got back, supporting me as I walked.

grounded_facts: Gus no longer sleeps in his basement or his own bed; he now sleeps in a hospital bed set up in a guest room.
memories.memory_text: I no longer sleep in my basement or my own bed—I’m in a hospital bed now, set up in the guest room.

grounded_facts: Gus and Hazel are spending time together watching sports on television in the guest room.
memories.memory_text: I’m spending time with Hazel in the guest room, and we’re watching sports on TV together.

grounded_facts: Hazel and Gus spend time together on the porch, seeking fresh air in a quiet moment.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting on the porch with Hazel, just taking in the fresh air while she read her book.

grounded_facts: Hazel waves to get Gus's attention, initiating connection.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Hazel waving at me, trying to get my attention.

grounded_facts: Gus holds Hazel's hand and mentally imagines a world without them, finding it worthless.

grounded_facts: Gus declares his deep love for Hazel and shares his belief that while pain is inevitable, one can choose who is allowed to cause it.
